  14    def __init__(
  15        self,
  16        CatsUserID: int = None,  # Deprecated - now read from environment
  17        data_path: str = "./data/",
  18        days_back: int = int(365 * 2),
  19        out_of_scope: list = [],
  20        testing: bool = False,
  21        coris_enabled: bool = False,
  22        conserv_enabled: bool = False,
  23        hobolink_enabled: bool = False,
  24    ):
  25        """
  26        Initialize resources for managing the environmental readings.
  27
  28        Parameters
  29        ----------
  30        CatsUserID : int, optional (deprecated)
  31            DEPRECATED: Cats User ID is now read from CATS_USER_ID environment variable.
  32            This parameter is maintained for backward compatibility but is ignored.
  33
  34        data_path : str, default='./data/'
  35            Path to store the parquet files which make up the database.
  36
  37        days_back : int, default=int(365 * 2)
  38            Number of days of historical data to pull when initializing the database.
  39
  40        out_of_scope : list[str], default=[]
  41            List of strings indicating sensors that are out of scope and should be ignored.
  42            If a SensorName starts with any of the strings in the list, that Sensor will be ignored.
  43
  44        testing : bool, default=False
  45            Create a class in "testing mode". Only a few sensors will be included so that tests can run quickly and use fewer API calls.
  46
  47        coris_enabled : bool, default=True
  48            Enable Coris API integration for primary sensor data source.
  49
  50        conserv_enabled : bool, default=False
  51            Enable Conserv API integration for additional sensor data sources.
  52
  53        hobolink_enabled : bool, default=False
  54            Enable Hobolink API integration for additional sensor data sources.
  55
  56        Returns
  57        -------
  58        EnvironmentData: EnvironmentData object.
  59        """
  60
  61        # Save inputs to the class instance.
  62        self.CatsUserID = CatsUserID  # Kept for backward compatibility
  63        self.data_path = data_path
  64        self.testing = testing
  65        self.testing_sensor_ids = []
  66        self.out_of_scope = out_of_scope
  67        self.coris_enabled = coris_enabled
  68        self.conserv_enabled = conserv_enabled
  69        self.hobolink_enabled = hobolink_enabled

  91            f"{data_path}/EnvironmentData.log"
  92        )  # log to EnvironmentData.log in the data folder.

  95
  96        # ch = logging.StreamHandler() # log to console. disabling to prevent breaking tdqm

 161
 162        # Initialize the database by creating a parquet file for each reading type and populate it with historical data.

 165    # function to update cron status.
 166    def update_cron_status(self, status: str):
 167        """
 168        cron_status is used to prevent new cron-triggered API queries during initialization while the historical data is being pulled. Update the status of the cron job.
 169        There are only two statuses: "not-initialized" and "initialized".
 170        This function updates the status by writing to "cron_status.txt" and setting the class instance variable self.cron_status.
 171
 172        Parameters
 173        ----------
 174        status : str {"not-initialized", "initialized"}
 175            New status of the cron job.
 176        """
 177
 178        self.cron_status = status
 179        with open(f"{self.data_path}/cron_status.txt", "w") as f:
 180            f.write(status)
 181
 182    def close(self):
 183        """
 184        Close the class.
 185        Disconnects the connection to the log files so they can be deleted, etc.
 186        """
 187
 188        for handler in self.logger.handlers:
 189            handler.close()
 190            self.logger.removeHandler(handler)
 191        del self.logger
 192
 193        for handler in self.logger_err.handlers:
 194            handler.close()
 195            self.logger_err.removeHandler(handler)
 196        del self.logger_err
 197
 198    def error(self, msg, raise_exception=False):
 199        """
 200        Helper function for errors.
 201        Logs an error message to the both log files (error regular) and raises an exception if you choose.
 202
 203        Parameters
 204        ----------
 205        msg : str
 206            Error message.
 207
 208        raise_exception : bool, default=False
 209            If True, log the error and raise an exception, which will halt processing. If False, log the error, generate a warning, and continue processing.
 210        """
 211
 212        self.logger_err.error(msg)
 213        self.logger.error(msg)
 214
 215        if raise_exception:
 216            raise Exception(msg)
 217        else:
 218            warnings.warn(msg)

 220    def initialize_database(self, days_back: int):
 221        """
 222        Get and save historical data for each sensor.
 223
 224        Parameters
 225        ----------
 226        days_back : int
 227            Number of days of historical data to pull.
 228        """
 229
 230        # If the data already exists, initialization is not necessary.
 231        if self.cron_status != "not-initialized":
 232            return
 233
 234        # Make a log entry and gather current and starting UTC.
 235        # self.logger.info("initialize_database")
 236        current_utc = self.get_current_utc()
 237        start_utc = current_utc - days_back * 24 * 60 * 60
 238
 239        # ============ CORIS HISTORICAL DATA PROCESSING ============
 240        readings = []
 241        if self.coris_enabled and self.coris_client:
 242            # Get historical data from Coris API using the client
 243            coris_readings = self.coris_client.get_historical_data(
 244                acceptable_range=self.acceptable_range,
 245                start_utc=start_utc,
 246                end_utc=current_utc,
 247                out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
 248                testing=self.testing,
 249                testing_sensor_ids=self.testing_sensor_ids
 250            )
 251
 252            # Clean and validate the Coris data
 253            for i, data in enumerate(coris_readings):
 254                coris_readings[i] = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 255                    sensors=data, step="initialize_database"
 256                )
 257            
 258            readings.extend(coris_readings)
 259
 260        # ============ CONSERV HISTORICAL DATA PROCESSING ============
 261        conserv_readings = []
 262        if self.conserv_enabled and self.conserv_client:
 263            self.logger.info("Fetching Conserv historical data for all customers")
 264
 265            try:
 266                # Get Conserv data for the same time period as Coris
 267                conserv_data = self.conserv_client.get_data_for_period(
 268                    start_utc=start_utc,
 269                    end_utc=current_utc,
 270                    max_concurrent_jobs=3 if self.testing else 5,
 271                )
 272
 273                if conserv_data is not None and not conserv_data.is_empty():
 274                    # Conserv data is already transformed by modules/conserv_client.py
 275                    # Clean and validate Conserv data
 276                    conserv_data = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 277                        sensors=conserv_data, step="initialize_database_conserv"
 278                    )
 279
 280                    # Add to readings list
 281                    conserv_readings.append(conserv_data)
 282                    self.logger.info(
 283                        f"Successfully processed {conserv_data.shape[0]} Conserv historical records"
 284                    )
 285                else:
 286                    self.logger.info(
 287                        "No Conserv historical data available for the specified period"
 288                    )
 289
 290            except Exception as e:
 291                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch Conserv historical data: {e}")
 292                # Continue without Conserv data - don't fail the entire initialization
 293
 294        # ============ HOBOLINK HISTORICAL DATA PROCESSING ============
 295        hobolink_readings = []
 296        if self.hobolink_enabled and self.hobolink_client:
 297            # print("DEBUG: Fetching Hobolink historical data")
 298            # self.logger.info("Fetching Hobolink historical data")
 299            
 300            try:
 301                # Get Hobolink data for the same time period
 302                hobolink_data_list = self.hobolink_client.get_historical_data(
 303                    start_utc=start_utc,
 304                    end_utc=current_utc,
 305                    out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
 306                    testing=self.testing
 307                )
 308                
 309                if hobolink_data_list is not None and len(hobolink_data_list) > 0:
 310                    # Clean and validate each DataFrame in the list
 311                    total_records = 0
 312                    for i, data in enumerate(hobolink_data_list):
 313                        if data is not None and not data.is_empty():
 314                            hobolink_data_list[i] = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 315                                sensors=data, step="initialize_database_hobolink"
 316                            )
 317                            total_records += hobolink_data_list[i].shape[0]
 318                    
 319                    # Add all DataFrames to readings list
 320                    hobolink_readings.extend(hobolink_data_list)
 321                    # print(f"DEBUG: Successfully processed {total_records} Hobolink historical records from {len(hobolink_data_list)} DataFrames")
 322                    # self.logger.info(
 323                    #     f"Successfully processed {total_records} Hobolink historical records from {len(hobolink_data_list)} DataFrames"
 324                    # )
 325                else:
 326                    print("DEBUG: No Hobolink historical data available for the specified period")
 327                    self.logger.info(
 328                        "No Hobolink historical data available for the specified period"
 329                    )
 330                    
 331            except Exception as e:
 332                print(f"DEBUG: Failed to fetch Hobolink historical data: {e}")
 333                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch Hobolink historical data: {e}")
 334                # Continue without Hobolink data - don't fail the entire initialization
 335        else:
 336            print(f"DEBUG: Hobolink not enabled or client not initialized. Enabled: {self.hobolink_enabled}, Client: {self.hobolink_client}")
 337
 338        # ============ COMBINE ALL DATA SOURCES ============
 339        # Combine Coris, Conserv, and Hobolink readings into a single polars DataFrame
 340        all_readings = readings + conserv_readings + hobolink_readings
 341        dt = (
 342            polars.concat(all_readings, how="diagonal")
 343            if all_readings
 344            else polars.DataFrame()
 345        )
 346
 347        if dt.is_empty():
 348            error_msg = "No data from any source - initialization failed"
 349            self.logger.error(error_msg)
 350            raise RuntimeError(error_msg)
 351
 352        # Standardize the DataFrame (rename columns, filter, and reorder)
 353        dt = self.standardize_sensor_dataframe(dt)
 354
 355        # Write the database file.
 356        dt.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet")
 357        self.logger.info(
 358            f"Historical data initialization complete: {dt.shape[0]} total records from {len(all_readings)} sources"
 359        )
 360
 361        self.update_cron_status("initialized")
 362

 365    def get_current_utc(self) -> int:

 452    def enforce_schema(
 453        self, df: polars.DataFrame, step_name: str = ""
 454    ) -> polars.DataFrame:
 455        """
 456        SCHEMA GATE: Enforce master schema on any DataFrame before concatenation.
 457        This prevents ALL type mismatch errors by converting data to expected types.
 458
 459        Parameters
 460        ----------
 461        df : polars.DataFrame
 462            DataFrame to enforce schema on
 463        step_name : str
 464            Name of the step for logging
 465
 466        Returns
 467        -------
 468        polars.DataFrame
 469            DataFrame with all columns converted to master schema types
 470        """
 471
 472        if df.is_empty():
 473            return df
 474
 475        master_schema = self.get_master_schema()
 476
 477        # Track conversions for logging
 478        conversions_made = []
 479
 480        # Apply schema enforcement
 481        conversion_exprs = []
 482        failed = False
 483
 484        for column in df.columns:
 485            if column in master_schema:
 486                target_type = master_schema[column]
 487                current_type = df[column].dtype
 488
 489                if current_type != target_type:
 490                    conversions_made.append(
 491                        f"{column}: {current_type} -> {target_type}"
 492                    )
 493
 494                    try:
 495                        # Handle specific conversion cases
 496                        if target_type == polars.Null:
 497                            # Keep null columns as-is
 498                            continue
 499                        elif str(current_type).startswith("Int") and str(
 500                            target_type
 501                        ).startswith("Int"):
 502                            # Int64 -> Int32 or vice versa (check for overflow)
 503                            conversion_exprs.append(
 504                                polars.col(column).cast(target_type, strict=False)
 505                            )
 506                        elif str(current_type).startswith("Float") and str(
 507                            target_type
 508                        ).startswith("Float"):
 509                            # Float64 -> Float32 or vice versa
 510                            conversion_exprs.append(
 511                                polars.col(column).cast(target_type)
 512                            )
 513                        else:
 514                            # Generic conversion
 515                            conversion_exprs.append(
 516                                polars.col(column).cast(target_type, strict=False)
 517                            )
 518
 519                    except Exception as conv_error:
 520                        self.logger.error(
 521                            f"Schema validation failed for {step_name}: Failed to convert {column}: {conv_error}"
 522                        )
 523                        failed = True
 524                        # Keep original column if conversion fails
 525                        continue
 526
 527        # Apply all conversions at once
 528        if conversion_exprs:
 529            df = df.with_columns(conversion_exprs)
 530
 531        if not failed:
 532            self.logger.info(f"validation passed for {step_name}: Schema enforcement completed")
 533
 534        return df
