 536    def get_current_readings(self) -> dict:
 537        """
 538        Get current readings from the API. Validate the data. Send alerts.
 539        Save the readings to a file in the new-readings folder.
 540        This function will save data as separate files to facilitate easy tracking of new data vs consolidated data.
 541        A batch process will clean, validate, and consolidate readings later.
 542        """
 543
 544        if self.cron_status == "not-initialized":
 545            return
 546
 547        # Make a log entry and gather the current UTC.
 548        current_utc = self.get_current_utc()
 549        # self.logger.info(f"get_current_readings: {current_utc}")
 550
 551        # ============ CORIS DATA PROCESSING ============
 552        coris_sensors = None
 553        if self.coris_enabled and self.coris_client:
 554            self.logger.info("Fetching current Coris data")
 555            
 556            # Get the current status from the Coris API using the client
 557            coris_sensors = self.coris_client.get_current_readings(
 558                out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
 559                testing=self.testing,
 560                testing_sensor_ids=self.testing_sensor_ids
 561            )
 562            
 563            # Convert data types to match expected schema before validation
 564            if not coris_sensors.is_empty():
 565                for reading in self.acceptable_range:
 566                    if reading in coris_sensors.columns:
 567                        coris_sensors = coris_sensors.with_columns(
 568                            polars.col(reading).cast(polars.Float32)
 569                        )
 570            
 571            self.validate_sensors(
 572                sensors=coris_sensors, utc=current_utc, step="get_current_readings_coris"
 573            )
 574        else:
 575            # Create empty DataFrame with required schema when Coris is disabled
 576            coris_sensors = polars.DataFrame()
 577            self.logger.info("Coris integration is disabled")
 578
 579        # DEBUG: Log Coris schema types
 580        # self.logger.info(
 581        #     f"CORIS schema types: {dict(zip(coris_sensors.columns, [str(dtype) for dtype in coris_sensors.dtypes]))}"
 582        # )
 583
 584        # ============ CONSERV DATA PROCESSING ============
 585        conserv_sensors = None
 586        if self.conserv_enabled and self.conserv_client:
 587            self.logger.info("Fetching current Conserv data for all customers")
 588
 589            try:
 590                # Get window size from environment (default 24 hours)
 591                def read_env_variable(var_name):
 592                    try:
 593                        with open(".env") as f:
 594                            for line in f:
 595                                if line.startswith(var_name):
 596                                    return line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
 597                    except FileNotFoundError:
 598                        pass
 599                    return None
 600
 601                hours_back = int(read_env_variable("RUN_WINDOW_HOURS") or "24")
 602                start_utc = current_utc - (
 603                    hours_back * 3600
 604                )  # Convert hours to seconds
 605
 606                # Get Conserv data for the specified window
 607                conserv_data = self.conserv_client.get_data_for_period(
 608                    start_utc=start_utc,
 609                    end_utc=current_utc,
 610                    max_concurrent_jobs=3 if self.testing else 5,
 611                )
 612
 613                if conserv_data is not None and not conserv_data.is_empty():
 614                    self.logger.info(f"Conserv data shape: {conserv_data.shape}")
 615
 616                    # Conserv data is already transformed by modules/conserv_client.py
 617                    conserv_sensors = conserv_data
 618
 619                    if conserv_sensors is not None and not conserv_sensors.is_empty():
 620                        # Clean and validate Conserv data
 621                        conserv_sensors = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 622                            sensors=conserv_sensors, step="get_current_readings_conserv"
 623                        )
 624
 625                        if (
 626                            conserv_sensors is not None
 627                            and not conserv_sensors.is_empty()
 628                        ):
 629                            self.logger.info(
 630                                f"Successfully processed {conserv_sensors.shape[0]} current Conserv records"
 631                            )
 632                        else:
 633                            self.logger.warning(
 634                                "Conserv data was cleaned out completely during validation!"
 635                            )
 636                    else:
 637                        self.logger.warning(
 638                            "Conserv transformation returned empty data!"
 639                        )
 640                else:
 641                    self.logger.info("No current Conserv data available")
 642
 643            except Exception as e:
 644                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch current Conserv data: {e}")
 645                import traceback
 646
 647                self.logger.warning(
 648                    f"Conserv error traceback: {traceback.format_exc()}"
 649                )
 650                # Continue with Coris data only - don't fail the entire process
 651
 652        # ============ HOBOLINK DATA PROCESSING ============
 653        hobolink_sensors = None
 654        if self.hobolink_enabled and self.hobolink_client:
 655            self.logger.info("Fetching current Hobolink data")
 656
 657            try:
 658                # Get current readings from Hobolink API
 659                hobolink_sensors = self.hobolink_client.get_current_readings(
 660                    out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
 661                    testing=self.testing,
 662                    testing_device_limit=3 if self.testing else None
 663                )
 664
 665                if hobolink_sensors is not None and not hobolink_sensors.is_empty():
 666                    self.logger.info(f"Raw Hobolink data shape: {hobolink_sensors.shape}")
 667
 668                    # Clean and validate Hobolink data
 669                    hobolink_sensors = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 670                        sensors=hobolink_sensors, step="get_current_readings_hobolink"
 671                    )
 672
 673                    if hobolink_sensors is not None and not hobolink_sensors.is_empty():
 674                        self.logger.info(
 675                            f"Successfully processed {hobolink_sensors.shape[0]} current Hobolink records"
 676                        )
 677                    else:
 678                        self.logger.warning(
 679                            "Hobolink data was cleaned out completely during validation!"
 680                        )
 681                else:
 682                    self.logger.info("No current Hobolink data available")
 683
 684            except Exception as e:
 685                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch current Hobolink data: {e}")
 686                import traceback
 687
 688                self.logger.warning(
 689                    f"Hobolink error traceback: {traceback.format_exc()}"
 690                )
 691                # Continue with other data sources - don't fail the entire process
 692
 693        # ============ COMBINE ALL DATA SOURCES ============
 694        # Prepare list of valid data sources for merging
 695        data_sources = []
 696        source_info = []
 697
 698        # Add Coris data if enabled and available
 699        if coris_sensors is not None and not coris_sensors.is_empty():
 700            coris_sensors = self.enforce_schema(coris_sensors, "Coris_Current_Readings")
 701            data_sources.append(coris_sensors)
 702            source_info.append(f"CORIS: {coris_sensors.shape[0]} rows")
 703
 704        if conserv_sensors is not None and not conserv_sensors.is_empty():
 705            conserv_sensors = self.enforce_schema(
 706                conserv_sensors, "Conserv_Current_Readings"
 707            )
 708            data_sources.append(conserv_sensors)
 709            source_info.append(f"CONSERV: {conserv_sensors.shape[0]} rows")
 710
 711        if hobolink_sensors is not None and not hobolink_sensors.is_empty():
 712            hobolink_sensors = self.enforce_schema(
 713                hobolink_sensors, "Hobolink_Current_Readings"
 714            )
 715            data_sources.append(hobolink_sensors)
 716            source_info.append(f"HOBOLINK: {hobolink_sensors.shape[0]} rows")
 717
 718        # Log merging information and combine data sources
 719        if len(data_sources) > 1:
 720            # self.logger.info("MERGING DATA SOURCES:")
 721            for info in source_info:
 722                self.logger.info(f"  {info}")
 723
 724            try:
 725                all_sensors = polars.concat(data_sources, how="diagonal")
 726                # total_rows = sum(df.shape[0] for df in data_sources)
 727                # self.logger.info(
 728                #     f"MERGE SUCCESS: Combined current readings from {len(data_sources)} sources = {all_sensors.shape[0]} total (expected: {total_rows})"
 729                # )
 730            except Exception as merge_error:
 731                self.logger.error(f"MERGE FAILED even with schema gate: {merge_error}")
 732                self.logger.error("Falling back to first available data source")
 733                all_sensors = data_sources[0] if data_sources else polars.DataFrame()
 734        elif len(data_sources) == 1:
 735            all_sensors = data_sources[0]
 736            self.logger.info(f"Current readings: {source_info[0]} only")
 737        else:
 738            # No data sources available
 739            all_sensors = polars.DataFrame()
 740            self.logger.warning("No data sources enabled or available - creating empty dataset")
 741
 742        # ============ PROCESS ALERTS AND SAVE ============
 743        # Process alerts on combined data
 744        self.send_alerts(all_sensors, current_utc)
 745
 746        # Standardize the current readings data (rename columns, filter, and reorder) 
 747        if not all_sensors.is_empty():
 748            # Include QueryUTC for current readings so it's preserved for later processing
 749            additional_columns = ["QueryUTC"] if "QueryUTC" in all_sensors.columns else []
 750            all_sensors = self.standardize_sensor_dataframe(all_sensors, include_additional_columns=additional_columns)
 751
 752        # Save the new-readings file. A daily process will pull these later to clean, validate, and consolidate them into the database.
 753        os.makedirs(f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/", exist_ok=True)
 754        all_sensors.write_parquet(
 755            f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/{current_utc}.parquet"
 756        )
 757
 758    def consolidate_readings(self):
 759        """
 760        Combine new and historical readings into one database. Build (or re-build) the analytical tables.
 761        If successful, remove the new-readings files that have been processed into the database.
 762        Meant to run as a daily batch process to consolidate readings made throughout the day.
 763        """
 764
 765        if self.cron_status == "not-initialized":
 766            return
 767
 768        # Make a log entry.
 769        # self.logger.info("consolidate_readings")
 770        new_readings = []
 771
 772        # Read new readings from the parquet files saved by calls to get_current_readings.
 773        # These are deleted after each consolidation, so these files will always be the un-consolidated files.
 774        files = os.listdir(f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/")
 775        files_read = []
 776        for file in files:
 777
 778            # Read any per-file parquet and collect them
 779            try:
 780                new_readings.append(
 781                    polars.read_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/{file}")
 782                )
 783                files_read.append(file)
 784            except Exception:
 785                # swallow and continue to the next file
 786                pass
 787
 788        # Combine the readings into a single polars DataFrame.
 789        dt = polars.concat(new_readings) if new_readings else polars.DataFrame()
 790        self.logger.info(f"{dt.shape[0]} new readings after schema enforcement.")
 791
 792        # Clean the data.
 793        try:
 794            historical = polars.read_parquet(
 795                f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet"
 796            )
 797        except FileNotFoundError:
 798            # Create empty DataFrame with correct schema for first run
 799            historical = polars.DataFrame()
 800
 801        dt = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 802            sensors=dt, historical=historical, step="consolidate_readings"
 803        )
 804
 805        # Apply schema gate before concatenating with historical data
 806        dt = self.enforce_schema(dt, "CleanedNewReadings")
 807        if not historical.is_empty():
 808            historical = self.enforce_schema(historical, "HistoricalData")
 809
 810        # Append these to the database.
 811        dt = polars.concat([historical, dt], how="diagonal")
 812
 813        # Add time difference between readings for each sensor
 814        if not dt.is_empty():
 815            dt = dt.sort(["SensorID", "SensorReadingUTC"])
 816            dt = dt.with_columns(
 817                (
 818                    polars.col("SensorReadingUTC")
 819                    - polars.col("SensorReadingUTC").shift(1).over("SensorID")
 820                ).alias("SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior")
 821            )
 822        else:
 823            dt = dt.with_columns(
 824                polars.lit(None, dtype=polars.Int64).alias(
 825                    "SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior"
 826                )
 827            )
 828
 829        # Standardize the DataFrame (rename columns, filter, and reorder)
 830        additional_columns = ["QueryUTC", "SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior"]
 831        dt = self.standardize_sensor_dataframe(dt, include_additional_columns=additional_columns)
 832
 833        # Write the file.
 834        dt.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet")
 835        # self.logger.info(f"{dt.shape[0]} total readings.")
 836
 837        # If all this was successful, remove the new-readings files to prepare for the next consolidation.
 838        for file in files_read:
 839            os.remove(f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/{file}")
 840
 841        # Refresh the devices table.
 842        devices = self.build_devices(dt)
 843        self.validate_devices(devices)
 844        devices.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/device_readings.parquet")
 845
 846        # Update lookup tables and cubes.
 847        self.update_lookups()
 848        self.update_cubes()
 849
 850    def match_types(
 851        self, data: polars.DataFrame, match: polars.DataFrame
 852    ) -> polars.DataFrame:
 853        """
 854        Modify the column data types of one DataFrame to match another.
 855        Useful to prevent errors during concatenation.
 856
 857        Parameters
 858        ----------
 859        data : polars.DataFrame
 860            DataFrame to match (data types may get changed).
 861
 862        match : polars.DataFrame
 863            DataFrame to match column data types to.
 864
 865        Returns
 866        -------
 867        polars.DataFrame: Same data as the "data" DataFrame, but with types that match the "match" DataFrame.
 868        """
 869
 870        for col in match.columns:
 871            if col in data.columns and data[col].dtype != match[col].dtype:
 872                data = data.with_columns(data[col].cast(match[col].dtype))
 873
 874        return data
 875
 876    def build_devices(self, data: polars.DataFrame) -> polars.DataFrame:
 877        """
 878        Reformat the sensor data to create a DataFrame of devices.
 879        Each Device can have multiple sensors.
 880        In some cases it is easier to work with data indexed by Device with multiple types of readings (Temperature, Humidity)
 881        in the same row instead of Sensors which only have one type of reading per row.
 882
 883        Parameters
 884        ----------
 885        data : polars.DataFrame
 886            DataFrame containing the sensor data.
 887
 888        Returns
 889        -------
 890        polars.DataFrame: DataFrame containing the devices data.
 891        """
 892
 893        # Get the data for each of the selected sensors.
 894        devices = None
 895        data = data.filter(polars.col("DeviceID").is_null().not_())
 896        for reading in self.acceptable_range:
 897            idt = data.filter(polars.col(reading).is_null().not_()).select(
 898                ["Source", "DeviceID", "SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC", reading]
 899            )
 900            if isinstance(devices, polars.DataFrame):
 901                devices = devices.join(
 902                    idt,
 903                    how="full",
 904                    on=["Source", "DeviceID", "SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC"],
 905                )
 906            else:
 907                devices = idt
 908            del idt, reading
 909
 910        # this will result in columns like DeviceID_right when there is not a perfect match.
 911        # coalesce to a single column.
 912        cols_Source = [x for x in devices.columns if "Source" in x]
 913        cols_DeviceID = [x for x in devices.columns if "DeviceID" in x]
 914        cols_SensorReadingUTC = [x for x in devices.columns if "SensorReadingUTC" in x]
 915        cols_QueryUTC = [x for x in devices.columns if "QueryUTC" in x]
 916
 917        devices = devices.with_columns(
 918            polars.coalesce(cols_Source).alias("Source")
 919        )
 920        devices = devices.with_columns(
 921            polars.coalesce(cols_DeviceID).alias("DeviceID")
 922        )
 923        devices = devices.with_columns(
 924            polars.coalesce(cols_SensorReadingUTC).alias("SensorReadingUTC")
 925        )
 926        devices = devices.with_columns(polars.coalesce(cols_QueryUTC).alias("QueryUTC"))
 927
 928        devices = devices.drop(
 929            [
 930                x
 931                for x in cols_Source + cols_DeviceID + cols_SensorReadingUTC + cols_QueryUTC
 932                if x not in ["Source", "DeviceID", "SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC"]
 933            ]
 934        )
 935
 936        # If a device has multiple names, error out:
 937        device_names = (
 938            data.filter(polars.col("DeviceID").is_null().not_())
 939            .select(["DeviceID", "DeviceName"])
 940            .unique()
 941        )
 942        if device_names.shape[0] != device_names["DeviceName"].unique().shape[0]:
 943            self.error(
 944                "DeviceName to DeviceID is not a 1-1 mapping.",
 945                raise_exception=True,
 946            )
 947
 948        # Attach the device name.
 949        devices = devices.join(device_names, how="left", on="DeviceID")
 950
 951        # Get sensor information for each device
 952        device_sensors = (
 953            data.filter(polars.col("DeviceID").is_null().not_())
 954            .select(["DeviceID", "SensorID", "SensorName", "SensorType"])
 955            .unique()
 956            .group_by("DeviceID")
 957            .agg([
 958                polars.col("SensorID").str.concat(", ").alias("Sensors"),
 959                polars.col("SensorName").str.concat(", ").alias("SensorNames"), 
 960                polars.col("SensorType").str.concat(", ").alias("SensorTypes")
 961            ])
 962        )
 963        
 964        # Join sensor information to devices
 965        devices = devices.join(device_sensors, how="left", on="DeviceID")
 966
 967        # Rearrange columns.
 968        devices = devices.select(
 969            ["Source", "DeviceID", "DeviceName", "Sensors", "SensorNames", "SensorTypes", "SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC"]
 970            + list(self.acceptable_range.keys())
 971        )
 972
 973        # Return the data.
 974        return devices
 975
 976    def clean_validate_sensors(
 977        self,
 978        sensors: polars.DataFrame,
 979        historical: polars.DataFrame = polars.DataFrame(),
 980        step: str = "",
 981    ) -> polars.DataFrame:
 982        """
 983        Clean the sensor readings data.
 984        Currently, this only sets efficient data types. It can be expanded to include more cleaning steps.
 985        Then, validate the data because these two operations typically occur together.
 986
 987        Parameters
 988        ----------
 989        sensors : polars.DataFrame
 990            Sensors API response.
 991
 992        Returns
 993        -------
 994        polars.DataFrame : Cleaned DataFrame.
 995        """
 996
 997        # Set data types - MATCH EXISTING SCHEMA EXACTLY
 998        dtypes = {
 999            "SensorID": polars.String,  # Consolidated sensor ID field with source prefixes
1000            "DeviceID": polars.String,  # Consolidated device ID field with source prefixes
1001            "SensorReadingUTC": polars.Int64,
1002            "QueryUTC": polars.Int32,  # Fixed: Match parquet file
1003            "Source": polars.String,  # Fixed: Use String not Utf8 (renamed from source)
1004        }
1005        
1006        # Add ConservCustomerID to dtypes only if Conserv is enabled
1007        if self.conserv_enabled:
1008            dtypes["ConservCustomerID"] = polars.Int32
1009        for dtype in dtypes:
1010            if dtype in sensors.columns:
1011                sensors = sensors.with_columns(polars.col(dtype).cast(dtypes[dtype]))
1012
1013        for reading in self.acceptable_range:
1014            if reading in sensors.columns:
1015                sensors = sensors.with_columns(
1016                    polars.col(reading).cast(polars.Float32)
1017                )  # Fixed: Use Float32 not String
1018
1019        # Also ensure validation expected columns are correct type
1020        validation_types = {
1021            "SensorReadingUTC": polars.Int64,
1022            "SensorID": polars.String,
1023            "SensorReadingF": polars.Float32,
1024            "SensorReadingRh": polars.Float32,
1025        }
1026        for col, expected_type in validation_types.items():
1027            if col in sensors.columns and sensors[col].dtype != expected_type:
1028                sensors = sensors.with_columns(polars.col(col).cast(expected_type))
1029                self.logger.info(f"Type conversion: {col} -> {expected_type}")
1030
1031        # Validate the data.
1032        self.validate_sensors(sensors=sensors, historical=historical, step=step)
1033
1034        return sensors
1035
1036    def standardize_sensor_dataframe(self, dt: polars.DataFrame, include_additional_columns: list = None) -> polars.DataFrame:
1037        """
1038        Standardize sensor data DataFrame by renaming columns, filtering, and reordering.
1039        
1040        Parameters
1041        ----------
1042        dt : polars.DataFrame
1043            Input DataFrame to standardize
1044        include_additional_columns : list, optional
1045            Additional columns to include after the standard columns
1046            
1047        Returns
1048        -------
1049        polars.DataFrame
1050            Standardized DataFrame with renamed columns, filtered columns, and proper ordering
1051        """
1052        # Rename columns to match desired schema
1053        column_renames = {}
1054        if "source" in dt.columns:
1055            column_renames["source"] = "Source"
1056        if "customer_id" in dt.columns:
1057            column_renames["customer_id"] = "ConservCustomerID"
1058        
1059        if column_renames:
1060            dt = dt.rename(column_renames)
1061
1062        # Remove ConservCustomerID column if Conserv is not enabled
1063        if not self.conserv_enabled and "ConservCustomerID" in dt.columns:
1064            dt = dt.drop("ConservCustomerID")
1065
1066        # Apply standard column ordering and filter to only desired columns
1067        desired_columns = self.get_sensor_readings_column_order()
1068        
1069        # Determine which columns to keep
1070        if include_additional_columns:
1071            all_columns = desired_columns + include_additional_columns
1072        else:
1073            all_columns = desired_columns
1074            
1075        # Only select columns that exist in both the data and the allowed columns
1076        available_columns = [col for col in all_columns if col in dt.columns]
1077        dt = dt.select(available_columns)
1078        
1079        return dt
1080
1081    def get_sensor_readings_column_order(self) -> list:
1082        """
1083        Get the standard column order for sensor_readings.parquet.
1084        
1085        Returns
1086        -------
1087        list[str] : Ordered list of column names
1088        """
1089        # Base columns in the desired order
1090        columns = [
1091            "SensorReadingUTC",
1092            "Source",  # Renamed from 'source' 
1093        ]
1094        
1095        # Add ConservCustomerID only if Conserv is enabled  
1096        if self.conserv_enabled:
1097            columns.append("ConservCustomerID")  # Renamed from 'customer_id'
1098            
1099        columns.extend([
1100            "DeviceID", 
1101            "DeviceName",
1102            "SensorID", 
1103            "SensorName", 
1104            "SensorType",
1105            "SensorReadingF", 
1106            "SensorReadingRh"
1107        ])
1108        
1109        return columns
1110
1111    def relocate(self, data: polars.DataFrame, columns: list) -> polars.DataFrame:
1112        """
1113        Helper function for relocating columns to the front of a DataFrame.
1114
1115        Parameters
1116        ----------
1117        data : polars.DataFrame
1118            DataFrame to relocate columns in.
1119
1120        columns : list[str]
1121            Columns to move to the front.
1122
1123        Returns
1124        -------
1125        polars.DataFrame : DataFrame with columns relocated.
1126        """
1127
1128        columns = [x for x in columns if x in data.columns]
1129        data = data[columns + [x for x in data.columns if x not in columns]]
1130        return data
1131
1132    def validate_sensors(
1133        self,
1134        sensors: polars.DataFrame,
1135        historical: polars.DataFrame = polars.DataFrame(),
1136        utc: int = None,
1137        step: str = "",
1138    ):
1139        """
1140        Validate Sensor reading data: column data types, missing values, SensorReadingUTC close to QueryUTC,
1141            no duplicated SensorReadingUTC, one SensorName per SensorID,
1142            SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior less than 15 minutes,
1143            all SensorID in historical data, no multiple names for SensorID.
1144        Can be expanded to add more validation steps.
1145        Failed validations are printed as errors to the log files, and surfaced as warnings.
1146
1147        Parameters
1148        ----------
1149        sensors: polars.DataFrame
1150            Sensor readings DataFrame to validate.
1151        """
1152
1153        errs = []
1154
1155        # We expect missing values in the data, so we don't check for them.
1156
1157        # Is the data format as expected?
1158        expect_types = {
1159            "SensorReadingUTC": polars.Int64,
1160            "SensorID": polars.String,
1161        }
1162        for reading in self.acceptable_range:
1163            if reading in sensors.columns:
1164                expect_types[reading] = (
1165                    polars.Float32
1166                )  # Fixed: Should be Float32 like existing data
1167
1168        type_errors_found = False
1169        for col in expect_types:
1170            if col in sensors.columns:
1171
1172                # data type.
1173                if sensors[col].dtype != expect_types[col]:
1174                    if not type_errors_found:
1175                        self.logger.info(f"{step} validation: correct column data types.")
1176                        type_errors_found = True
1177                    errs.append(
1178                        f"Unexpected data type for [{col}]. Expected [{expect_types[col]}] got [{sensors[col]}]."
1179                    )
1180
1181        # Readings should have at least one non-null value from expect_types.
1182        allnull = sensors[[x for x in expect_types if x in sensors.columns]].filter(
1183            polars.all_horizontal(polars.all().is_null())
1184        )
1185        missing_count = allnull.shape[0]
1186        if missing_count > 0:
1187            self.logger.info(f"{step} validation: at least one non-null value in readings.")
1188            # Note: Missing values are expected in sensor data (e.g., temperature-only vs humidity-only sensors)
1189            # errs.append(f"{missing_count} missing values in [{col}].")
1190
1191        # Are the SensorReadingUTC close to the QueryUTC (the time the data was requested via API)?
1192        if utc is not None:
1193            maxdiff_minutes = (
1194                numpy.max(numpy.abs(sensors["SensorReadingUTC"].to_numpy() - utc)) / 60
1195            )
1196            if maxdiff_minutes > 5: # readings should be happening every 2 minutes.
1197                errs.append(
1198                    f"SensorReadingUTC is {maxdiff_minutes:,.0f} minutes old"
1199                )
1200            else:                
1201                self.logger.info(
1202                    f"{step} validation passed: SensorReadingUTC columns close to QueryUTC."
1203                )
1204
1205        # Are there any duplicated SensorReadingUTC per SensorID?
1206        if "SensorReadingUTC" in sensors.columns:
1207            dup_count = (
1208                sensors[["SensorID", "SensorReadingUTC"]].is_duplicated().sum()
1209            )
1210            if dup_count > 0:
1211                errs.append(f"Count of duplicated SensorReadingUTC: {dup_count}.")
1212            else:                
1213                self.logger.info(
1214                    f"{step} validation passed: no duplicated SensorReadingUTC per SensorID."
1215                )
1216
1217        # Do any sensors have multiple names (indicating a change in name)?
1218        name_dups = sensors[["SensorID", "SensorName"]].unique()
1219        name_dups = name_dups.filter(name_dups["SensorID"].is_duplicated())
1220        dup_count = name_dups[["SensorID"]].unique().shape[0]
1221        if dup_count > 0:
1222            errs.append(f"Count of multiple names for SensorID: {dup_count}.")
1223        else:            
1224            self.logger.info(f"{step} validation passed: one SensorName per SensorID.")
1225
1226        # Time between readings should be less than ten minutes.
1227        if "SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior" in sensors.columns:
1228            badrows = sensors.filter(
1229                sensors["SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior"] > 60 * 15
1230            )
1231            if badrows.shape[0] > 0:
1232                errs.append(
1233                    f"Count of SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior > 15 minutes: {badrows.shape[0]}."
1234                )
1235            else:                
1236                self.logger.info(
1237                    f"{step} validation passed: SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior less than 15 minutes."
1238                )
1239
1240        # Comparisons to historical.
1241        if historical.shape[0] > 0:
1242
1243            # Did we lose any sensors?
1244            missing = historical.filter(
1245                historical["SensorID"].is_in(sensors["SensorID"]).not_()
1246            )
1247            if missing.shape[0] > 0:
1248                errs.append(
1249                    f"Count of sensors missing from historical data: {missing.shape[0]}."
1250                )
1251            else:
1252                self.logger.info(
1253                    f"{step} validation passed: all SensorID in historical data (no dropped SensorID)."
1254                )
1255
1256        # Log the errors.
1257        if len(errs) > 0:
1258            self.error(
1259                step + " validation errors : " + "; ".join(errs) + "\n",
1260                raise_exception=False,
1261            )
1262
1263    def validate_devices(self, devices: polars.DataFrame):
1264        """
1265        Validate Device data: column data types, missing values.
1266        Can be expanded to add more validation steps.
1267
1268        Parameters
1269        ----------
1270        devices: polars.DataFrame
1271            Device readings DataFrame to validate.
1272        """
1273
1274        errs = []
1275
1276        # Check for missing values.
1277        # Note: Missing values are expected in sensor data (e.g., temperature-only vs humidity-only sensors)
1278        # for col in self.acceptable_range:
1279        #     missing_count = devices[col].is_null().sum()
1280        #     if missing_count > 0:
1281        #         errs.append(f"{missing_count} missing values in [{col}].")
1282
1283        # Log the errors.
1284        if len(errs) > 0:
1285            self.error(
1286                "Validation errors: \n" + "\n\t".join(errs), raise_exception=False
1287            )
1288
1289    def which(x):
1290        return list(numpy.where(x)[0])
1291
1292    def send_alerts(self, sensors: polars.DataFrame, utc: int):
1293        """
1294        Send alerts based on the sensor data.
1295        Currently, this function saves alerts to "alerts.txt" in the data folder.
1296        Later, this can be connected to an messaging system like Twilio.
1297
1298        Parameters
1299        ----------
1300        sensors: polars.DataFrame
1301            Sensor readings DataFrame.
1302
1303        utc: int
1304            Current UTC timestamp. Passed from another function to keep alerts aligned with QueryUTC.
1305        """
1306
1307        alerts = []
1308        for reading in self.acceptable_range:
1309
1310            if len(self.acceptable_range[reading]) == 0:
1311                continue
1312
1313            reading_idx = self.which(sensors.columns == reading)
1314
1315            for i, row in sensors.iter_rows():
1316                if (not not row[reading_idx].is_null()) and (
1317                    row[reading_idx] < self.acceptable_range[reading][0]
1318                    or row[reading] > self.acceptable_range[reading][1]
1319                ):
1320                    alerts.append(row)
1321
1322        # Write the alerts to a file.
1323        # Later, this can be connected to an alerting system like Twilio.
1324        if len(alerts) > 0:
1325            with open(f"{self.data_path}/alerts.txt", "w") as f:
1326                f.write("\n".join(alerts))
1327
1328    def update_lookups(self):
1329        """
1330        Build (or re-build) the lookup tables used for analytical queries using the consolidated parquet files: sensors, devices, and utcs.
1331        """
1332
1333        # We need some manual fixes to reformat invalid names.
1334        name_overrides = {
1335            "980D Unnamed Temp Sensor": "Temp Unnamed Unnamed_980D",
1336            "980D Unnamed Humid Sensor": "RH Unnamed Unnamed_980D",
1337        }
1338
1339        building_name_map = {
1340            "ESC": "Environmental Science Center",
1341            "YPM": "Yale Peabody Museum",
1342            "KGL": "Kline Geology Laboratory",
1343            "CSC": "Collection Studies Center (West Campus)",
1344        }
1345
1346        # Sensor Info.
1347        columns_to_read = [
1348            "SensorName",
1349            "SensorID",
1350            "DeviceID",
1351            "SensorType",
1352            "Source",
1353        ]
1354        if self.conserv_enabled:
1355            columns_to_read.append("ConservCustomerID")
1356            
1357        sensors_data = polars.read_parquet(
1358            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet",
1359            columns=columns_to_read,
1360        )
1361        sensors_data = sensors_data.unique().to_dicts()
1362        sensors = []
1363        for sensor in sensors_data:
1364
1365            sensorname = sensor["SensorName"]
1366            # Skip processing if SensorName is None/null
1367            if sensorname is None:
1368                continue
1369                
1370            if sensorname in name_overrides:
1371                sensorname = name_overrides[sensorname]
1372
1373            # Fix sensor names with problematic prefixes by removing everything up to and including the first space
1374            if "__" in sensorname and " " in sensorname:
1375                sensorname = sensorname[sensorname.index(" ") + 1:]
1376
1377            # Fix sensor names with " - no comm" suffix
1378            if " - no comm" in sensorname:
1379                sensorname = sensorname.replace(" - no comm", "")
1380
1381            if "floator" in sensorname.lower():
1382                info = sensorname.strip().split("_")
1383            else:
1384                info = sensorname.strip().split(" ")
1385                info = info[0:-1] + info[-1].split("_")
1386            
1387            # Clean up empty strings from consecutive separators (e.g., multiple underscores)
1388            info = [part for part in info if part.strip() != ""]
1389
1390            # If the cardinal direction is included, there will be 4 pieces of info.
1391            if len(info) == 5:
1392                sensors.append(
1393                    {
1394                        "Source": sensor["Source"],
1395                        "SensorName": sensorname,
1396                        #   'SensorType_fromName': info[0],
1397                        "DeviceSerialFromName": info[4],
1398                        "SensorType": sensor["SensorType"],
1399                        "SensorID": sensor["SensorID"],
1400                        "DeviceID": sensor["DeviceID"],
1401                        "BuildingID": info[1],
1402                        "Building": (
1403                            building_name_map[info[1]]
1404                            if info[1] in building_name_map
1405                            else "Unknown"
1406                        ),
1407                        "Room": info[2].replace("_", ""),
1408                        "CardinalDirection": info[3],
1409                    }
1410                )
1411                if info[1] not in building_name_map:
1412                    self.logger.warning(
1413                        f"Building ID {info[1]} not found in building_name_map for sensor {sensorname}"
1414                    )
1415
1416            elif len(info) == 4:
1417
1418                sensors.append(
1419                    {
1420                        "Source": sensor["Source"],
1421                        "SensorName": sensorname,
1422                        #'SensorType_fromName': info[0],
1423                        "DeviceSerialFromName": info[3],
1424                        "SensorType": sensor["SensorType"],
1425                        "SensorID": sensor["SensorID"],
1426                        "DeviceID": sensor["DeviceID"],
1427                        "BuildingID": info[1],
1428                        "Building": (
1429                            building_name_map[info[1]]
1430                            if info[1] in building_name_map
1431                            else "Unknown"
1432                        ),
1433                        "Room": info[2].replace("_", ""),
1434                        "CardinalDirection": "Not Indicated",
1435                    }
1436                )
1437                if info[1] not in building_name_map:
1438                    self.logger.warning(
1439                        f"Building ID {info[1]} not found in building_name_map for sensor {sensorname}"
1440                    )
1441
1442            # Floaters are len 3.
1443            elif len(info) == 3:
1444                sensors.append(
1445                    {
1446                        "Source": sensor["Source"],
1447                        "SensorName": sensorname,
1448                        # 'SensorType_fromName': info[0],
1449                        "DeviceSerialFromName": info[2],
1450                        "SensorType": sensor["SensorType"],
1451                        "SensorID": sensor["SensorID"],
1452                        "DeviceID": sensor["DeviceID"],
1453                        "BuildingID": "FLOATER",
1454                        "Building": (
1455                            building_name_map[info[1]]
1456                            if info[1] in building_name_map
1457                            else "Unknown"
1458                        ),
1459                        "Room": "FLOATER",
1460                        "CardinalDirection": None,
1461                    }
1462                )
1463            else:
1464                # Handle malformed sensor names gracefully with NAs
1465                self.logger.warning(
1466                    f"Malformed SensorName format: {sensorname}. Info: {info}. "
1467                    f"Adding with NA values for parsed fields. "
1468                    f"Valid formats: "
1469                    f"'Temp ESC Room101 North_1234' (5 parts with cardinal direction), "
1470                    f"'RH YPM Gallery_2567' (4 parts without cardinal direction), "
1471                    f"'Temp_Floater ESC_3890' (3 parts for floaters)"
1472                )
1473                sensors.append(
1474                    {
1475                        "Source": sensor["Source"],
1476                        "SensorName": sensorname,
1477                        "DeviceSerialFromName": None,  # NA for malformed names
1478                        "SensorType": sensor["SensorType"],
1479                        "SensorID": sensor["SensorID"], 
1480                        "DeviceID": sensor["DeviceID"],
1481                        "BuildingID": "MALFORMED",
1482                        "Building": "Unknown",
1483                        "Room": "Unknown", 
1484                        "CardinalDirection": None,
1485                    }
1486                )
1487
1488        # Write the table to a file.
1489        sensors = polars.DataFrame(sensors).unique()
1490        sensors = sensors.sort(
1491            ["BuildingID", "Building", "Room", "DeviceSerialFromName", "SensorName"]
1492        )
1493        sensors = self.clean_validate_sensors(sensors=sensors, step="update_lookups")
1494        sensors = self.relocate(
1495            sensors,
1496            ["Source", "SensorID", "SensorName", "SensorType", "DeviceID", "DeviceSerialFromName", "BuildingID", "Building", "Room", "CardinalDirection"],
1497        )
1498        sensors.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/sensors.parquet")
1499
1500        # It will be helpful to have the Building, Room, and CardinalDirection appended to Devices.
1501        # Check for a valid mapping.
1502        device_info_from_sensors = sensors.select(
1503            [
1504                "DeviceID",
1505                "BuildingID",
1506                "Building",
1507                "Room",
1508                "CardinalDirection",
1509                "DeviceSerialFromName",
1510            ]
1511        ).unique()
1512
1513        # Check for inconsistent DeviceID mappings (same DeviceID with different Building/Room/CardinalDirection)
1514        # Group by DeviceID and check if there are multiple unique combinations of Building/Room/CardinalDirection
1515        device_consistency_check = device_info_from_sensors.group_by("DeviceID").agg([
1516            polars.col("BuildingID").n_unique().alias("unique_buildings"),
1517            polars.col("Room").n_unique().alias("unique_rooms"), 
1518            polars.col("CardinalDirection").n_unique().alias("unique_directions")
1519        ])
1520        
1521        inconsistent_devices = device_consistency_check.filter(
1522            (polars.col("unique_buildings") > 1) |
1523            (polars.col("unique_rooms") > 1) |
1524            (polars.col("unique_directions") > 1)
1525        )
1526
1527        if inconsistent_devices.shape[0] > 0:
1528            # Get the actual inconsistent mappings for logging
1529            bad_device_ids = inconsistent_devices.select("DeviceID").to_series().to_list()
1530            bad_values = device_info_from_sensors.filter(
1531                polars.col("DeviceID").is_in(bad_device_ids)
1532            ).sort("DeviceID")
1533            
1534            self.logger.warning(
1535                f"DeviceID has inconsistent Building/Room/CardinalDirection mappings. Using first occurrence: \n{bad_values}"
1536            )
1537            
1538            # Keep only the first occurrence of each DeviceID to maintain consistency
1539            device_info_from_sensors = device_info_from_sensors.group_by("DeviceID").first()
1540        else:
1541            # If all mappings are consistent, we can still have multiple rows per DeviceID (for different sensor types)
1542            # Just keep one representative row per DeviceID since Building/Room/CardinalDirection should be the same
1543            device_info_from_sensors = device_info_from_sensors.group_by("DeviceID").first()
1544
1545        # Device Info.
1546        devices = polars.read_parquet(
1547            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet",
1548            columns=["Source", "DeviceID", "DeviceName"],
1549        ).unique()
1550        devices = devices.join(
1551            device_info_from_sensors, how="left", on="DeviceID"
1552        ).sort(["BuildingID", "Room", "DeviceName"])
1553        
1554        # Get sensor information for each device from the sensors lookup table
1555        device_sensors_lookup = sensors.group_by("DeviceID").agg([
1556            polars.col("SensorID").str.concat(", ").alias("Sensors"),
1557            polars.col("SensorName").str.concat(", ").alias("SensorNames"),
1558            polars.col("SensorType").str.concat(", ").alias("SensorTypes")
1559        ])
1560        
1561        # Join sensor information to devices
1562        devices = devices.join(device_sensors_lookup, how="left", on="DeviceID")
1563        
1564        devices = self.relocate(
1565            devices,
1566            ["Source", "DeviceID", "DeviceName", "Sensors", "SensorNames", "SensorTypes", "DeviceSerialFromName", "BuildingID", "Building", "Room", "CardinalDirection"],
1567        )
1568        devices.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/devices.parquet")
1569
1570        # UTC info.
1571        # Get all UTC timestamps from sensor_readings: both SensorReadingUTC and QueryUTC
1572        # sensor_readings is the primary source since all other data derives from it
1573        
1574        # Read both SensorReadingUTC and QueryUTC columns
1575        utc_data = polars.read_parquet(
1576            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet", 
1577            columns=["SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC"]
1578        )
1579        
1580        # Get SensorReadingUTC values (remove nulls)
1581        sensor_reading_utcs = (
1582            utc_data.filter(polars.col("SensorReadingUTC").is_not_null())
1583            ["SensorReadingUTC"]
1584            .unique()
1585            .to_list()
1586        )
1587        
1588        # Get QueryUTC values (remove nulls) 
1589        query_utcs = (
1590            utc_data.filter(polars.col("QueryUTC").is_not_null())
1591            ["QueryUTC"]
1592            .unique()
1593            .to_list()
1594        )
1595        
1596        # Combine all UTC timestamps and get unique values
1597        utc_timestamps = list(set(sensor_reading_utcs + query_utcs))
1598
1599        utcs = polars.DataFrame(
1600            {
1601                "UTC": utc_timestamps,
1602                "datetime_utc": [
1603                    datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(x) for x in utc_timestamps
1604                ],
1605            }
1606        )
1607
1608        # Convert to EST and round to seconds.
1609        utcs = utcs.with_columns(
1610            polars.col("datetime_utc")
1611            .dt.convert_time_zone("America/New_York")
1612            .dt.round("1s")
1613            .alias("datetime_est")
1614        )
1615
1616        # Extract all the date parts.
1617        utcs = utcs.with_columns(
1618            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.date().alias("date"),
1619            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.time().alias("time"),
1620            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.year().alias("year"),
1621            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.month().alias("month"),
1622            (polars.col("datetime_est").dt.strftime("%A")).alias("day_of_week"),
1623            polars.col("datetime_est")
1624            .dt.weekday()
1625            .alias("day_of_week_monday1_sunday7"),
1626            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.hour().alias("hour_24"),
1627            (polars.col("datetime_est").dt.hour() % 12).alias("hour_12"),
1628            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.strftime("%p").alias("am_pm"),
1629        )
1630
1631        # Write the table to a file.
1632        utcs.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/utcs.parquet")
1633
1634    def update_cubes(self):
1635        """
1636        Build (or re-build) the cubed tables using the consolidated parquet files.
1637        Cubes contain aggregated measures by day and device/sensor to facilitate faster queries on smaller files.
1638        In the future, cubes can be modified to include different aggregation levels and dimensions.
1639        """
1640
1641        sumcols = list(self.acceptable_range.keys())
1642        utcs = polars.read_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/utcs.parquet")
1643
1644        sensor_readings = polars.read_parquet(
1645            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet"
1646        )
1647        sensor_readings = sensor_readings.filter(
1648            polars.col("QueryUTC").is_null() | 
1649            ((polars.col("SensorReadingUTC") - polars.col("QueryUTC")).abs() < 60 * 5)
1650        )  # include historical data (QueryUTC=null) and recent readings within 5min window
1651        sensor_readings = sensor_readings.join(
1652            utcs[["UTC", "date"]],
1653            how="left",
1654            left_on="SensorReadingUTC",
1655            right_on="UTC",
1656        )
1657
1658        sensor_readings_daily = (
1659            sensor_readings.group_by(["Source", "date", "SensorID"])
1660            .agg(
1661                [
1662                    polars.len().alias("row_count"),
1663                    polars.col(sumcols).sum().name.suffix("_sum"),
1664                    polars.col(sumcols).min().name.suffix("_min"),
1665                    polars.col(sumcols).max().name.suffix("_max"),
1666                ]
1667            )
1668            .sort(["Source", "date", "SensorID"])
1669        )
1670
1671        sensor_readings_daily.write_parquet(
1672            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings_daily.parquet"
1673        )
1674
1675        device_readings = polars.read_parquet(
1676            f"{self.data_path}/device_readings.parquet"
1677        )
1678        device_readings = device_readings.filter(
1679            polars.col("QueryUTC").is_null() | 
1680            ((polars.col("SensorReadingUTC") - polars.col("QueryUTC")).abs() < 60 * 5)
1681        )  # include historical data (QueryUTC=null) and recent readings within 5min window
1682        device_readings = device_readings.join(
1683            utcs[["UTC", "date"]],
1684            how="left",
1685            left_on="SensorReadingUTC",
1686            right_on="UTC",
1687        )
1688
1689        device_readings_daily = (
1690            device_readings.group_by(["Source", "date", "DeviceID"])
1691            .agg(
1692                [
1693                    polars.len().alias("row_count"),
1694                    polars.col(sumcols).sum().name.suffix("_sum"),
1695                    polars.col(sumcols).min().name.suffix("_min"),
1696                    polars.col(sumcols).max().name.suffix("_max"),
1697                ]
1698            )
1699            .sort(["Source", "date", "DeviceID"])
1700        )
1701
1702        device_readings_daily.write_parquet(
1703            f"{self.data_path}/device_readings_daily.parquet"
1704        )
class EnvironmentData: 
  13class EnvironmentData:
  14
  15    def __init__(
  16        self,
  17        CatsUserID: int = None,  # Deprecated - now read from environment
  18        data_path: str = "./data/",
  19        days_back: int = int(365 * 2),
  20        out_of_scope: list = [],
  21        testing: bool = False,
  22        coris_enabled: bool = False,
  23        conserv_enabled: bool = False,
  24        hobolink_enabled: bool = False,
  25    ):
  26        """
  27        Initialize resources for managing the environmental readings.
  28
  29        Parameters
  30        ----------
  31        CatsUserID : int, optional (deprecated)
  32            DEPRECATED: Cats User ID is now read from CATS_USER_ID environment variable.
  33            This parameter is maintained for backward compatibility but is ignored.
  34
  35        data_path : str, default='./data/'
  36            Path to store the parquet files which make up the database.
  37
  38        days_back : int, default=int(365 * 2)
  39            Number of days of historical data to pull when initializing the database.
  40
  41        out_of_scope : list[str], default=[]
  42            List of strings indicating sensors that are out of scope and should be ignored.
  43            If a SensorName starts with any of the strings in the list, that Sensor will be ignored.
  44
  45        testing : bool, default=False
  46            Create a class in "testing mode". Only a few sensors will be included so that tests can run quickly and use fewer API calls.
  47
  48        coris_enabled : bool, default=True
  49            Enable Coris API integration for primary sensor data source.
  50
  51        conserv_enabled : bool, default=False
  52            Enable Conserv API integration for additional sensor data sources.
  53
  54        hobolink_enabled : bool, default=False
  55            Enable Hobolink API integration for additional sensor data sources.
  56
  57        Returns
  58        -------
  59        EnvironmentData: EnvironmentData object.
  60        """
  61
  62        # Save inputs to the class instance.
  63        self.CatsUserID = CatsUserID  # Kept for backward compatibility
  64        self.data_path = data_path
  65        self.testing = testing
  66        self.testing_sensor_ids = []
  67        self.out_of_scope = out_of_scope
  68        self.coris_enabled = coris_enabled
  69        self.conserv_enabled = conserv_enabled
  70        self.hobolink_enabled = hobolink_enabled
  71
  72        # Check that at least one data source is enabled
  73        if not (coris_enabled or conserv_enabled or hobolink_enabled):
  74            raise ValueError(
  75                "At least one data source must be enabled. "
  76                "Set coris_enabled=True, conserv_enabled=True, or hobolink_enabled=True"
  77            )
  78
  79        # Create the data folder.
  80        if not os.path.exists(data_path):
  81            os.makedirs(data_path)
  82
  83        # Set up logging to allow status to be viewed when run as a cron job.
  84        # https://docs.python.org/3/howto/logging-cookbook.html#logging-cookbook
  85        self.logger = logging.getLogger("EnvironmentData")
  86        self.logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
  87        formatter = logging.Formatter(
  88            "%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"
  89        )
  90
  91        fh = logging.FileHandler(
  92            f"{data_path}/EnvironmentData.log"
  93        )  # log to EnvironmentData.log in the data folder.
  94        fh.setFormatter(formatter)
  95        self.logger.addHandler(fh)
  96
  97        # ch = logging.StreamHandler() # log to console. disabling to prevent breaking tdqm
  98        # ch.setFormatter(formatter)
  99        # self.logger.addHandler(ch)
 100
 101        # Set up a second logger for errors only.
 102        self.logger_err = logging.getLogger("EnvironmentData-Errors")
 103        self.logger_err.setLevel(logging.ERROR)
 104        fh = logging.FileHandler(f"{data_path}/EnvironmentData-Errors.log")
 105        fh.setFormatter(formatter)
 106        self.logger_err.addHandler(fh)
 107
 108        # Read cron status, or initialize the status file.
 109        if os.path.exists(f"{data_path}/cron_status.txt"):
 110            with open(f"{data_path}/cron_status.txt") as f:
 111                self.cron_status = f.read()
 112        else:
 113            self.update_cron_status("not-initialized")
 114
 115        # Initialize Coris API client if enabled
 116        self.coris_client = None
 117        if self.coris_enabled:
 118            try:
 119                self.coris_client = create_coris_client_from_env(self.logger)
 120                # self.logger.info("Coris API client initialized successfully")
 121            except Exception as e:
 122                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to initialize Coris client: {e}")
 123                self.coris_enabled = False
 124
 125        # Initialize Conserv API client if enabled
 126        self.conserv_client = None
 127        if self.conserv_enabled:
 128            try:
 129                self.conserv_client = create_conserv_client_from_env(self.logger)
 130                # self.logger.info(
 131                #     f"Conserv API client initialized with {len(self.conserv_client.customers)} customers"
 132                # )
 133            except Exception as e:
 134                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to initialize Conserv client: {e}")
 135                self.conserv_enabled = False
 136
 137        # Initialize Hobolink API client if enabled
 138        self.hobolink_client = None
 139        if self.hobolink_enabled:
 140            try:
 141                self.hobolink_client = HobolinkClient(self.logger)
 142                # self.logger.info("Hobolink API client initialized successfully")
 143            except Exception as e:
 144                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to initialize Hobolink client: {e}")
 145                print(f"DEBUG: Failed to initialize Hobolink client: {e}")
 146                self.hobolink_enabled = False
 147
 148        # Set up the readings data structure that will be used throughout.
 149        self.acceptable_range = {"SensorReadingF": [], "SensorReadingRh": []}
 150
 151        # Debug: Show which data sources are actually enabled
 152        enabled_sources = []
 153        if self.coris_enabled and self.coris_client:
 154            enabled_sources.append("Coris")
 155        if self.conserv_enabled and self.conserv_client:
 156            enabled_sources.append("Conserv") 
 157        if self.hobolink_enabled and self.hobolink_client:
 158            enabled_sources.append("Hobolink")
 159        
 160        print(f"DEBUG: Enabled data sources: {enabled_sources}")
 161        self.logger.info(f"Enabled data sources: {enabled_sources}")
 162
 163        # Initialize the database by creating a parquet file for each reading type and populate it with historical data.
 164        self.initialize_database(days_back=days_back)
 165
 166    # function to update cron status.
 167    def update_cron_status(self, status: str):
 168        """
 169        cron_status is used to prevent new cron-triggered API queries during initialization while the historical data is being pulled. Update the status of the cron job.
 170        There are only two statuses: "not-initialized" and "initialized".
 171        This function updates the status by writing to "cron_status.txt" and setting the class instance variable self.cron_status.
 172
 173        Parameters
 174        ----------
 175        status : str {"not-initialized", "initialized"}
 176            New status of the cron job.
 177        """
 178
 179        self.cron_status = status
 180        with open(f"{self.data_path}/cron_status.txt", "w") as f:
 181            f.write(status)
 182
 183    def close(self):
 184        """
 185        Close the class.
 186        Disconnects the connection to the log files so they can be deleted, etc.
 187        """
 188
 189        for handler in self.logger.handlers:
 190            handler.close()
 191            self.logger.removeHandler(handler)
 192        del self.logger
 193
 194        for handler in self.logger_err.handlers:
 195            handler.close()
 196            self.logger_err.removeHandler(handler)
 197        del self.logger_err
 198
 199    def error(self, msg, raise_exception=False):
 200        """
 201        Helper function for errors.
 202        Logs an error message to the both log files (error regular) and raises an exception if you choose.
 203
 204        Parameters
 205        ----------
 206        msg : str
 207            Error message.
 208
 209        raise_exception : bool, default=False
 210            If True, log the error and raise an exception, which will halt processing. If False, log the error, generate a warning, and continue processing.
 211        """
 212
 213        self.logger_err.error(msg)
 214        self.logger.error(msg)
 215
 216        if raise_exception:
 217            raise Exception(msg)
 218        else:
 219            warnings.warn(msg)
 220
 221    def initialize_database(self, days_back: int):
 222        """
 223        Get and save historical data for each sensor.
 224
 225        Parameters
 226        ----------
 227        days_back : int
 228            Number of days of historical data to pull.
 229        """
 230
 231        # If the data already exists, initialization is not necessary.
 232        if self.cron_status != "not-initialized":
 233            return
 234
 235        # Make a log entry and gather current and starting UTC.
 236        # self.logger.info("initialize_database")
 237        current_utc = self.get_current_utc()
 238        start_utc = current_utc - days_back * 24 * 60 * 60
 239
 240        # ============ CORIS HISTORICAL DATA PROCESSING ============
 241        readings = []
 242        if self.coris_enabled and self.coris_client:
 243            # Get historical data from Coris API using the client
 244            coris_readings = self.coris_client.get_historical_data(
 245                acceptable_range=self.acceptable_range,
 246                start_utc=start_utc,
 247                end_utc=current_utc,
 248                out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
 249                testing=self.testing,
 250                testing_sensor_ids=self.testing_sensor_ids
 251            )
 252
 253            # Clean and validate the Coris data
 254            for i, data in enumerate(coris_readings):
 255                coris_readings[i] = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 256                    sensors=data, step="initialize_database"
 257                )
 258            
 259            readings.extend(coris_readings)
 260
 261        # ============ CONSERV HISTORICAL DATA PROCESSING ============
 262        conserv_readings = []
 263        if self.conserv_enabled and self.conserv_client:
 264            self.logger.info("Fetching Conserv historical data for all customers")
 265
 266            try:
 267                # Get Conserv data for the same time period as Coris
 268                conserv_data = self.conserv_client.get_data_for_period(
 269                    start_utc=start_utc,
 270                    end_utc=current_utc,
 271                    max_concurrent_jobs=3 if self.testing else 5,
 272                )
 273
 274                if conserv_data is not None and not conserv_data.is_empty():
 275                    # Conserv data is already transformed by modules/conserv_client.py
 276                    # Clean and validate Conserv data
 277                    conserv_data = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 278                        sensors=conserv_data, step="initialize_database_conserv"
 279                    )
 280
 281                    # Add to readings list
 282                    conserv_readings.append(conserv_data)
 283                    self.logger.info(
 284                        f"Successfully processed {conserv_data.shape[0]} Conserv historical records"
 285                    )
 286                else:
 287                    self.logger.info(
 288                        "No Conserv historical data available for the specified period"
 289                    )
 290
 291            except Exception as e:
 292                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch Conserv historical data: {e}")
 293                # Continue without Conserv data - don't fail the entire initialization
 294
 295        # ============ HOBOLINK HISTORICAL DATA PROCESSING ============
 296        hobolink_readings = []
 297        if self.hobolink_enabled and self.hobolink_client:
 298            # print("DEBUG: Fetching Hobolink historical data")
 299            # self.logger.info("Fetching Hobolink historical data")
 300            
 301            try:
 302                # Get Hobolink data for the same time period
 303                hobolink_data_list = self.hobolink_client.get_historical_data(
 304                    start_utc=start_utc,
 305                    end_utc=current_utc,
 306                    out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
 307                    testing=self.testing
 308                )
 309                
 310                if hobolink_data_list is not None and len(hobolink_data_list) > 0:
 311                    # Clean and validate each DataFrame in the list
 312                    total_records = 0
 313                    for i, data in enumerate(hobolink_data_list):
 314                        if data is not None and not data.is_empty():
 315                            hobolink_data_list[i] = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 316                                sensors=data, step="initialize_database_hobolink"
 317                            )
 318                            total_records += hobolink_data_list[i].shape[0]
 319                    
 320                    # Add all DataFrames to readings list
 321                    hobolink_readings.extend(hobolink_data_list)
 322                    # print(f"DEBUG: Successfully processed {total_records} Hobolink historical records from {len(hobolink_data_list)} DataFrames")
 323                    # self.logger.info(
 324                    #     f"Successfully processed {total_records} Hobolink historical records from {len(hobolink_data_list)} DataFrames"
 325                    # )
 326                else:
 327                    print("DEBUG: No Hobolink historical data available for the specified period")
 328                    self.logger.info(
 329                        "No Hobolink historical data available for the specified period"
 330                    )
 331                    
 332            except Exception as e:
 333                print(f"DEBUG: Failed to fetch Hobolink historical data: {e}")
 334                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch Hobolink historical data: {e}")
 335                # Continue without Hobolink data - don't fail the entire initialization
 336        else:
 337            print(f"DEBUG: Hobolink not enabled or client not initialized. Enabled: {self.hobolink_enabled}, Client: {self.hobolink_client}")
 338
 339        # ============ COMBINE ALL DATA SOURCES ============
 340        # Combine Coris, Conserv, and Hobolink readings into a single polars DataFrame
 341        all_readings = readings + conserv_readings + hobolink_readings
 342        dt = (
 343            polars.concat(all_readings, how="diagonal")
 344            if all_readings
 345            else polars.DataFrame()
 346        )
 347
 348        if dt.is_empty():
 349            error_msg = "No data from any source - initialization failed"
 350            self.logger.error(error_msg)
 351            raise RuntimeError(error_msg)
 352
 353        # Standardize the DataFrame (rename columns, filter, and reorder)
 354        dt = self.standardize_sensor_dataframe(dt)
 355
 356        # Write the database file.
 357        dt.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet")
 358        self.logger.info(
 359            f"Historical data initialization complete: {dt.shape[0]} total records from {len(all_readings)} sources"
 360        )
 361
 362        self.update_cron_status("initialized")
 363
 364
 365
 366    def get_current_utc(self) -> int:
 367        """
 368        Get the current UTC timestamp in seconds.
 369
 370        Returns
 371        -------
 372        int : Current UTC timestamp.
 373        """
 374
 375        return int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp())

 413            "UserTempPref": polars.String,

 418            "SensorState1String": polars.String,
 419            "ExpectedSensorReadingIntervalSeconds": polars.Int64,
 420            "SensorReadingC": polars.Float64,
 421            "SensorCalibrationOffsetC": polars.Float64,
 422            "SensorCalibrationOffsetF": polars.Float64,
 423            "SensorCalibrationOffsetExplanationText": polars.String,
 424            "SensorCalibrationOffsetExplanationFirstName": polars.String,
 425            "SensorCalibrationOffsetExplanationLastName": polars.String,
 426            "SensorCalibrationOffsetUTC": polars.Int64,
 427            "LoraBatteryPresent": polars.Int64,
 428            "LoraBattery_mV": polars.Int64,

 445        }

 447        # Add ConservCustomerID to schema only if Conserv is enabled
 448        if self.conserv_enabled:

 451        return master_schema
