 453    def enforce_schema(
 454        self, df: polars.DataFrame, step_name: str = ""
 455    ) -> polars.DataFrame:
 456        """
 457        SCHEMA GATE: Enforce master schema on any DataFrame before concatenation.
 458        This prevents ALL type mismatch errors by converting data to expected types.
 459
 460        Parameters
 461        ----------
 462        df : polars.DataFrame
 463            DataFrame to enforce schema on
 464        step_name : str
 465            Name of the step for logging
 466
 467        Returns
 468        -------
 469        polars.DataFrame
 470            DataFrame with all columns converted to master schema types
 471        """
 472
 473        if df.is_empty():
 474            return df
 475
 476        master_schema = self.get_master_schema()
 477
 478        # Track conversions for logging
 479        conversions_made = []
 480
 481        # Apply schema enforcement
 482        conversion_exprs = []
 483        failed = False
 484
 485        for column in df.columns:
 486            if column in master_schema:
 487                target_type = master_schema[column]
 488                current_type = df[column].dtype
 489
 490                if current_type != target_type:
 491                    conversions_made.append(
 492                        f"{column}: {current_type} -> {target_type}"
 493                    )
 494
 495                    try:
 496                        # Handle specific conversion cases
 497                        if target_type == polars.Null:
 498                            # Keep null columns as-is
 499                            continue
 500                        elif str(current_type).startswith("Int") and str(
 501                            target_type
 502                        ).startswith("Int"):
 503                            # Int64 -> Int32 or vice versa (check for overflow)
 504                            conversion_exprs.append(
 505                                polars.col(column).cast(target_type, strict=False)
 506                            )
 507                        elif str(current_type).startswith("Float") and str(
 508                            target_type
 509                        ).startswith("Float"):
 510                            # Float64 -> Float32 or vice versa
 511                            conversion_exprs.append(
 512                                polars.col(column).cast(target_type)
 513                            )
 514                        else:
 515                            # Generic conversion
 516                            conversion_exprs.append(
 517                                polars.col(column).cast(target_type, strict=False)
 518                            )
 519
 520                    except Exception as conv_error:
 521                        self.logger.error(
 522                            f"Schema validation failed for {step_name}: Failed to convert {column}: {conv_error}"
 523                        )
 524                        failed = True
 525                        # Keep original column if conversion fails
 526                        continue
 527
 528        # Apply all conversions at once
 529        if conversion_exprs:
 530            df = df.with_columns(conversion_exprs)
 531
 532        if not failed:
 533            self.logger.info(f"validation passed for {step_name}: Schema enforcement completed")
 534
 535        return df
 536
 537    def get_current_readings(self) -> dict:
 538        """
 539        Get current readings from the API. Validate the data. Send alerts.
 540        Save the readings to a file in the new-readings folder.
 541        This function will save data as separate files to facilitate easy tracking of new data vs consolidated data.
 542        A batch process will clean, validate, and consolidate readings later.
 543        """
 544
 545        if self.cron_status == "not-initialized":
 546            return
 547
 548        # Make a log entry and gather the current UTC.
 549        current_utc = self.get_current_utc()
 550        # self.logger.info(f"get_current_readings: {current_utc}")
 551
 552        # ============ CORIS DATA PROCESSING ============
 553        coris_sensors = None
 554        if self.coris_enabled and self.coris_client:
 555            self.logger.info("Fetching current Coris data")
 556            
 557            # Get the current status from the Coris API using the client
 558            coris_sensors = self.coris_client.get_current_readings(
 559                out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
 560                testing=self.testing,
 561                testing_sensor_ids=self.testing_sensor_ids
 562            )
 563            
 564            # Convert data types to match expected schema before validation
 565            if not coris_sensors.is_empty():
 566                for reading in self.acceptable_range:
 567                    if reading in coris_sensors.columns:
 568                        coris_sensors = coris_sensors.with_columns(
 569                            polars.col(reading).cast(polars.Float32)
 570                        )
 571            
 572            self.validate_sensors(
 573                sensors=coris_sensors, utc=current_utc, step="get_current_readings_coris"
 574            )
 575        else:
 576            # Create empty DataFrame with required schema when Coris is disabled
 577            coris_sensors = polars.DataFrame()
 578            self.logger.info("Coris integration is disabled")
 579
 580        # DEBUG: Log Coris schema types
 581        # self.logger.info(
 582        #     f"CORIS schema types: {dict(zip(coris_sensors.columns, [str(dtype) for dtype in coris_sensors.dtypes]))}"
 583        # )
 584
 585        # ============ CONSERV DATA PROCESSING ============
 586        conserv_sensors = None
 587        if self.conserv_enabled and self.conserv_client:
 588            self.logger.info("Fetching current Conserv data for all customers")
 589
 590            try:
 591                # Get window size from environment (default 24 hours)
 592                def read_env_variable(var_name):
 593                    try:
 594                        with open(".env") as f:
 595                            for line in f:
 596                                if line.startswith(var_name):
 597                                    return line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
 598                    except FileNotFoundError:
 599                        pass
 600                    return None
 601
 602                hours_back = int(read_env_variable("RUN_WINDOW_HOURS") or "24")
 603                start_utc = current_utc - (
 604                    hours_back * 3600
 605                )  # Convert hours to seconds
 606
 607                # Get Conserv data for the specified window
 608                conserv_data = self.conserv_client.get_data_for_period(
 609                    start_utc=start_utc,
 610                    end_utc=current_utc,
 611                    max_concurrent_jobs=3 if self.testing else 5,
 612                )
 613
 614                if conserv_data is not None and not conserv_data.is_empty():
 615                    self.logger.info(f"Conserv data shape: {conserv_data.shape}")
 616
 617                    # Conserv data is already transformed by modules/conserv_client.py
 618                    conserv_sensors = conserv_data
 619
 620                    if conserv_sensors is not None and not conserv_sensors.is_empty():
 621                        # Clean and validate Conserv data
 622                        conserv_sensors = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 623                            sensors=conserv_sensors, step="get_current_readings_conserv"
 624                        )
 625
 626                        if (
 627                            conserv_sensors is not None
 628                            and not conserv_sensors.is_empty()
 629                        ):
 630                            self.logger.info(
 631                                f"Successfully processed {conserv_sensors.shape[0]} current Conserv records"
 632                            )
 633                        else:
 634                            self.logger.warning(
 635                                "Conserv data was cleaned out completely during validation!"
 636                            )
 637                    else:
 638                        self.logger.warning(
 639                            "Conserv transformation returned empty data!"
 640                        )
 641                else:
 642                    self.logger.info("No current Conserv data available")
 643
 644            except Exception as e:
 645                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch current Conserv data: {e}")
 646                import traceback
 647
 648                self.logger.warning(
 649                    f"Conserv error traceback: {traceback.format_exc()}"
 650                )
 651                # Continue with Coris data only - don't fail the entire process
 652
 653        # ============ HOBOLINK DATA PROCESSING ============
 654        hobolink_sensors = None
 655        if self.hobolink_enabled and self.hobolink_client:
 656            self.logger.info("Fetching current Hobolink data")
 657
 658            try:
 659                # Get current readings from Hobolink API
 660                hobolink_sensors = self.hobolink_client.get_current_readings(
 661                    out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
 662                    testing=self.testing,
 663                    testing_device_limit=3 if self.testing else None
 664                )
 665
 666                if hobolink_sensors is not None and not hobolink_sensors.is_empty():
 667                    self.logger.info(f"Raw Hobolink data shape: {hobolink_sensors.shape}")
 668
 669                    # Clean and validate Hobolink data
 670                    hobolink_sensors = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 671                        sensors=hobolink_sensors, step="get_current_readings_hobolink"
 672                    )
 673
 674                    if hobolink_sensors is not None and not hobolink_sensors.is_empty():
 675                        self.logger.info(
 676                            f"Successfully processed {hobolink_sensors.shape[0]} current Hobolink records"
 677                        )
 678                    else:
 679                        self.logger.warning(
 680                            "Hobolink data was cleaned out completely during validation!"
 681                        )
 682                else:
 683                    self.logger.info("No current Hobolink data available")
 684
 685            except Exception as e:
 686                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch current Hobolink data: {e}")
 687                import traceback
 688
 689                self.logger.warning(
 690                    f"Hobolink error traceback: {traceback.format_exc()}"
 691                )
 692                # Continue with other data sources - don't fail the entire process
 693
 694        # ============ COMBINE ALL DATA SOURCES ============
 695        # Prepare list of valid data sources for merging
 696        data_sources = []
 697        source_info = []
 698
 699        # Add Coris data if enabled and available
 700        if coris_sensors is not None and not coris_sensors.is_empty():
 701            coris_sensors = self.enforce_schema(coris_sensors, "Coris_Current_Readings")
 702            data_sources.append(coris_sensors)
 703            source_info.append(f"CORIS: {coris_sensors.shape[0]} rows")
 704
 705        if conserv_sensors is not None and not conserv_sensors.is_empty():
 706            conserv_sensors = self.enforce_schema(
 707                conserv_sensors, "Conserv_Current_Readings"
 708            )
 709            data_sources.append(conserv_sensors)
 710            source_info.append(f"CONSERV: {conserv_sensors.shape[0]} rows")
 711
 712        if hobolink_sensors is not None and not hobolink_sensors.is_empty():
 713            hobolink_sensors = self.enforce_schema(
 714                hobolink_sensors, "Hobolink_Current_Readings"
 715            )
 716            data_sources.append(hobolink_sensors)
 717            source_info.append(f"HOBOLINK: {hobolink_sensors.shape[0]} rows")
 718
 719        # Log merging information and combine data sources
 720        if len(data_sources) > 1:
 721            # self.logger.info("MERGING DATA SOURCES:")
 722            for info in source_info:
 723                self.logger.info(f"  {info}")
 724
 725            try:
 726                all_sensors = polars.concat(data_sources, how="diagonal")
 727                # total_rows = sum(df.shape[0] for df in data_sources)
 728                # self.logger.info(
 729                #     f"MERGE SUCCESS: Combined current readings from {len(data_sources)} sources = {all_sensors.shape[0]} total (expected: {total_rows})"
 730                # )
 731            except Exception as merge_error:
 732                self.logger.error(f"MERGE FAILED even with schema gate: {merge_error}")
 733                self.logger.error("Falling back to first available data source")
 734                all_sensors = data_sources[0] if data_sources else polars.DataFrame()
 735        elif len(data_sources) == 1:
 736            all_sensors = data_sources[0]
 737            self.logger.info(f"Current readings: {source_info[0]} only")
 738        else:
 739            # No data sources available
 740            all_sensors = polars.DataFrame()
 741            self.logger.warning("No data sources enabled or available - creating empty dataset")
 742
 743        # ============ PROCESS ALERTS AND SAVE ============
 744        # Process alerts on combined data
 745        self.send_alerts(all_sensors, current_utc)
 746
 747        # Standardize the current readings data (rename columns, filter, and reorder) 
 748        if not all_sensors.is_empty():
 749            # Include QueryUTC for current readings so it's preserved for later processing
 750            additional_columns = ["QueryUTC"] if "QueryUTC" in all_sensors.columns else []
 751            all_sensors = self.standardize_sensor_dataframe(all_sensors, include_additional_columns=additional_columns)
 752
 753        # Save the new-readings file. A daily process will pull these later to clean, validate, and consolidate them into the database.
 754        os.makedirs(f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/", exist_ok=True)
 755        all_sensors.write_parquet(
 756            f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/{current_utc}.parquet"
 757        )
 758
 759    def consolidate_readings(self):
 760        """
 761        Combine new and historical readings into one database. Build (or re-build) the analytical tables.
 762        If successful, remove the new-readings files that have been processed into the database.
 763        Meant to run as a daily batch process to consolidate readings made throughout the day.
 764        """
 765
 766        if self.cron_status == "not-initialized":
 767            return
 768
 769        # Make a log entry.
 770        # self.logger.info("consolidate_readings")
 771        new_readings = []
 772
 773        # Read new readings from the parquet files saved by calls to get_current_readings.
 774        # These are deleted after each consolidation, so these files will always be the un-consolidated files.
 775        files = os.listdir(f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/")
 776        files_read = []
 777        for file in files:
 778
 779            # Read any per-file parquet and collect them
 780            try:
 781                new_readings.append(
 782                    polars.read_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/{file}")
 783                )
 784                files_read.append(file)
 785            except Exception:
 786                # swallow and continue to the next file
 787                pass
 788
 789        # Combine the readings into a single polars DataFrame.
 790        dt = polars.concat(new_readings) if new_readings else polars.DataFrame()
 791        self.logger.info(f"{dt.shape[0]} new readings after schema enforcement.")
 792
 793        # Clean the data.
 794        try:
 795            historical = polars.read_parquet(
 796                f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet"
 797            )
 798        except FileNotFoundError:
 799            # Create empty DataFrame with correct schema for first run
 800            historical = polars.DataFrame()
 801
 802        dt = self.clean_validate_sensors(
 803            sensors=dt, historical=historical, step="consolidate_readings"
 804        )
 805
 806        # Apply schema gate before concatenating with historical data
 807        dt = self.enforce_schema(dt, "CleanedNewReadings")
 808        if not historical.is_empty():
 809            historical = self.enforce_schema(historical, "HistoricalData")
 810
 811        # Append these to the database.
 812        dt = polars.concat([historical, dt], how="diagonal")
 813
 814        # Add time difference between readings for each sensor
 815        if not dt.is_empty():
 816            dt = dt.sort(["SensorID", "SensorReadingUTC"])
 817            dt = dt.with_columns(
 818                (
 819                    polars.col("SensorReadingUTC")
 820                    - polars.col("SensorReadingUTC").shift(1).over("SensorID")
 821                ).alias("SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior")
 822            )
 823        else:
 824            dt = dt.with_columns(
 825                polars.lit(None, dtype=polars.Int64).alias(
 826                    "SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior"
 827                )
 828            )
 829
 830        # Standardize the DataFrame (rename columns, filter, and reorder)
 831        additional_columns = ["QueryUTC", "SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior"]
 832        dt = self.standardize_sensor_dataframe(dt, include_additional_columns=additional_columns)
 833
 834        # Write the file.
 835        dt.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet")
 836        # self.logger.info(f"{dt.shape[0]} total readings.")
 837
 838        # If all this was successful, remove the new-readings files to prepare for the next consolidation.
 839        for file in files_read:
 840            os.remove(f"{self.data_path}/new-readings/{file}")
 841
 842        # Refresh the devices table.
 843        devices = self.build_devices(dt)
 844        self.validate_devices(devices)
 845        devices.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/device_readings.parquet")
 846
 847        # Update lookup tables and cubes.
 848        self.update_lookups()
 849        self.update_cubes()
 850
 851    def match_types(
 852        self, data: polars.DataFrame, match: polars.DataFrame
 853    ) -> polars.DataFrame:
 854        """
 855        Modify the column data types of one DataFrame to match another.
 856        Useful to prevent errors during concatenation.
 857
 858        Parameters
 859        ----------
 860        data : polars.DataFrame
 861            DataFrame to match (data types may get changed).
 862
 863        match : polars.DataFrame
 864            DataFrame to match column data types to.
 865
 866        Returns
 867        -------
 868        polars.DataFrame: Same data as the "data" DataFrame, but with types that match the "match" DataFrame.
 869        """
 870
 871        for col in match.columns:
 872            if col in data.columns and data[col].dtype != match[col].dtype:
 873                data = data.with_columns(data[col].cast(match[col].dtype))
 874
 875        return data
 876
 877    def build_devices(self, data: polars.DataFrame) -> polars.DataFrame:
 878        """
 879        Reformat the sensor data to create a DataFrame of devices.
 880        Each Device can have multiple sensors.
 881        In some cases it is easier to work with data indexed by Device with multiple types of readings (Temperature, Humidity)
 882        in the same row instead of Sensors which only have one type of reading per row.
 883
 884        Parameters
 885        ----------
 886        data : polars.DataFrame
 887            DataFrame containing the sensor data.
 888
 889        Returns
 890        -------
 891        polars.DataFrame: DataFrame containing the devices data.
 892        """
 893
 894        # Get the data for each of the selected sensors.
 895        devices = None
 896        data = data.filter(polars.col("DeviceID").is_null().not_())
 897        for reading in self.acceptable_range:
 898            idt = data.filter(polars.col(reading).is_null().not_()).select(
 899                ["Source", "DeviceID", "SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC", reading]
 900            )
 901            if isinstance(devices, polars.DataFrame):
 902                devices = devices.join(
 903                    idt,
 904                    how="full",
 905                    on=["Source", "DeviceID", "SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC"],
 906                )
 907            else:
 908                devices = idt
 909            del idt, reading
 910
 911        # this will result in columns like DeviceID_right when there is not a perfect match.
 912        # coalesce to a single column.
 913        cols_Source = [x for x in devices.columns if "Source" in x]
 914        cols_DeviceID = [x for x in devices.columns if "DeviceID" in x]
 915        cols_SensorReadingUTC = [x for x in devices.columns if "SensorReadingUTC" in x]
 916        cols_QueryUTC = [x for x in devices.columns if "QueryUTC" in x]
 917
 918        devices = devices.with_columns(
 919            polars.coalesce(cols_Source).alias("Source")
 920        )
 921        devices = devices.with_columns(
 922            polars.coalesce(cols_DeviceID).alias("DeviceID")
 923        )
 924        devices = devices.with_columns(
 925            polars.coalesce(cols_SensorReadingUTC).alias("SensorReadingUTC")
 926        )
 927        devices = devices.with_columns(polars.coalesce(cols_QueryUTC).alias("QueryUTC"))
 928
 929        devices = devices.drop(
 930            [
 931                x
 932                for x in cols_Source + cols_DeviceID + cols_SensorReadingUTC + cols_QueryUTC
 933                if x not in ["Source", "DeviceID", "SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC"]
 934            ]
 935        )
 936
 937        # If a device has multiple names, error out:
 938        device_names = (
 939            data.filter(polars.col("DeviceID").is_null().not_())
 940            .select(["DeviceID", "DeviceName"])
 941            .unique()
 942        )
 943        if device_names.shape[0] != device_names["DeviceName"].unique().shape[0]:
 944            self.error(
 945                "DeviceName to DeviceID is not a 1-1 mapping.",
 946                raise_exception=True,
 947            )
 948
 949        # Attach the device name.
 950        devices = devices.join(device_names, how="left", on="DeviceID")
 951
 952        # Get sensor information for each device
 953        device_sensors = (
 954            data.filter(polars.col("DeviceID").is_null().not_())
 955            .select(["DeviceID", "SensorID", "SensorName", "SensorType"])
 956            .unique()
 957            .group_by("DeviceID")
 958            .agg([
 959                polars.col("SensorID").str.concat(", ").alias("Sensors"),
 960                polars.col("SensorName").str.concat(", ").alias("SensorNames"), 
 961                polars.col("SensorType").str.concat(", ").alias("SensorTypes")
 962            ])
 963        )
 964        
 965        # Join sensor information to devices
 966        devices = devices.join(device_sensors, how="left", on="DeviceID")
 967
 968        # Rearrange columns.
 969        devices = devices.select(
 970            ["Source", "DeviceID", "DeviceName", "Sensors", "SensorNames", "SensorTypes", "SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC"]
 971            + list(self.acceptable_range.keys())
 972        )
 973
 974        # Return the data.
 975        return devices
 976
 977    def clean_validate_sensors(
 978        self,
 979        sensors: polars.DataFrame,
 980        historical: polars.DataFrame = polars.DataFrame(),
 981        step: str = "",
 982    ) -> polars.DataFrame:
 983        """
 984        Clean the sensor readings data.
 985        Currently, this only sets efficient data types. It can be expanded to include more cleaning steps.
 986        Then, validate the data because these two operations typically occur together.
 987
 988        Parameters
 989        ----------
 990        sensors : polars.DataFrame
 991            Sensors API response.
 992
 993        Returns
 994        -------
 995        polars.DataFrame : Cleaned DataFrame.
 996        """
 997
 998        # Set data types - MATCH EXISTING SCHEMA EXACTLY
 999        dtypes = {
1000            "SensorID": polars.String,  # Consolidated sensor ID field with source prefixes
1001            "DeviceID": polars.String,  # Consolidated device ID field with source prefixes
1002            "SensorReadingUTC": polars.Int64,
1003            "QueryUTC": polars.Int32,  # Fixed: Match parquet file
1004            "Source": polars.String,  # Fixed: Use String not Utf8 (renamed from source)
1005        }
1006        
1007        # Add ConservCustomerID to dtypes only if Conserv is enabled
1008        if self.conserv_enabled:
1009            dtypes["ConservCustomerID"] = polars.Int32
1010        for dtype in dtypes:
1011            if dtype in sensors.columns:
1012                sensors = sensors.with_columns(polars.col(dtype).cast(dtypes[dtype]))
1013
1014        for reading in self.acceptable_range:
1015            if reading in sensors.columns:
1016                sensors = sensors.with_columns(
1017                    polars.col(reading).cast(polars.Float32)
1018                )  # Fixed: Use Float32 not String
1019
1020        # Also ensure validation expected columns are correct type
1021        validation_types = {
1022            "SensorReadingUTC": polars.Int64,
1023            "SensorID": polars.String,
1024            "SensorReadingF": polars.Float32,
1025            "SensorReadingRh": polars.Float32,
1026        }
1027        for col, expected_type in validation_types.items():
1028            if col in sensors.columns and sensors[col].dtype != expected_type:
1029                sensors = sensors.with_columns(polars.col(col).cast(expected_type))
1030                self.logger.info(f"Type conversion: {col} -> {expected_type}")
1031
1032        # Validate the data.
1033        self.validate_sensors(sensors=sensors, historical=historical, step=step)
1034
1035        return sensors
1036
1037    def standardize_sensor_dataframe(self, dt: polars.DataFrame, include_additional_columns: list = None) -> polars.DataFrame:
1038        """
1039        Standardize sensor data DataFrame by renaming columns, filtering, and reordering.
1040        
1041        Parameters
1042        ----------
1043        dt : polars.DataFrame
1044            Input DataFrame to standardize
1045        include_additional_columns : list, optional
1046            Additional columns to include after the standard columns
1047            
1048        Returns
1049        -------
1050        polars.DataFrame
1051            Standardized DataFrame with renamed columns, filtered columns, and proper ordering
1052        """
1053        # Rename columns to match desired schema
1054        column_renames = {}
1055        if "source" in dt.columns:
1056            column_renames["source"] = "Source"
1057        if "customer_id" in dt.columns:
1058            column_renames["customer_id"] = "ConservCustomerID"
1059        
1060        if column_renames:
1061            dt = dt.rename(column_renames)
1062
1063        # Remove ConservCustomerID column if Conserv is not enabled
1064        if not self.conserv_enabled and "ConservCustomerID" in dt.columns:
1065            dt = dt.drop("ConservCustomerID")
1066
1067        # Apply standard column ordering and filter to only desired columns
1068        desired_columns = self.get_sensor_readings_column_order()
1069        
1070        # Determine which columns to keep
1071        if include_additional_columns:
1072            all_columns = desired_columns + include_additional_columns
1073        else:
1074            all_columns = desired_columns
1075            
1076        # Only select columns that exist in both the data and the allowed columns
1077        available_columns = [col for col in all_columns if col in dt.columns]
1078        dt = dt.select(available_columns)
1079        
1080        return dt
1081
1082    def get_sensor_readings_column_order(self) -> list:
1083        """
1084        Get the standard column order for sensor_readings.parquet.
1085        
1086        Returns
1087        -------
1088        list[str] : Ordered list of column names
1089        """
1090        # Base columns in the desired order
1091        columns = [
1092            "SensorReadingUTC",
1093            "Source",  # Renamed from 'source' 
1094        ]
1095        
1096        # Add ConservCustomerID only if Conserv is enabled  
1097        if self.conserv_enabled:
1098            columns.append("ConservCustomerID")  # Renamed from 'customer_id'
1099            
1100        columns.extend([
1101            "DeviceID", 
1102            "DeviceName",
1103            "SensorID", 
1104            "SensorName", 
1105            "SensorType",
1106            "SensorReadingF", 
1107            "SensorReadingRh"
1108        ])
1109        
1110        return columns
1111
1112    def relocate(self, data: polars.DataFrame, columns: list) -> polars.DataFrame:
1113        """
1114        Helper function for relocating columns to the front of a DataFrame.
1115
1116        Parameters
1117        ----------
1118        data : polars.DataFrame
1119            DataFrame to relocate columns in.
1120
1121        columns : list[str]
1122            Columns to move to the front.
1123
1124        Returns
1125        -------
1126        polars.DataFrame : DataFrame with columns relocated.
1127        """
1128
1129        columns = [x for x in columns if x in data.columns]
1130        data = data[columns + [x for x in data.columns if x not in columns]]
1131        return data
1132
1133    def validate_sensors(
1134        self,
1135        sensors: polars.DataFrame,
1136        historical: polars.DataFrame = polars.DataFrame(),
1137        utc: int = None,
1138        step: str = "",
1139    ):
1140        """
1141        Validate Sensor reading data: column data types, missing values, SensorReadingUTC close to QueryUTC,
1142            no duplicated SensorReadingUTC, one SensorName per SensorID,
1143            SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior less than 15 minutes,
1144            all SensorID in historical data, no multiple names for SensorID.
1145        Can be expanded to add more validation steps.
1146        Failed validations are printed as errors to the log files, and surfaced as warnings.
1147
1148        Parameters
1149        ----------
1150        sensors: polars.DataFrame
1151            Sensor readings DataFrame to validate.
1152        """
1153
1154        errs = []
1155
1156        # We expect missing values in the data, so we don't check for them.
1157
1158        # Is the data format as expected?
1159        expect_types = {
1160            "SensorReadingUTC": polars.Int64,
1161            "SensorID": polars.String,
1162        }
1163        for reading in self.acceptable_range:
1164            if reading in sensors.columns:
1165                expect_types[reading] = (
1166                    polars.Float32
1167                )  # Fixed: Should be Float32 like existing data
1168
1169        type_errors_found = False
1170        for col in expect_types:
1171            if col in sensors.columns:
1172
1173                # data type.
1174                if sensors[col].dtype != expect_types[col]:
1175                    if not type_errors_found:
1176                        self.logger.info(f"{step} validation: correct column data types.")
1177                        type_errors_found = True
1178                    errs.append(
1179                        f"Unexpected data type for [{col}]. Expected [{expect_types[col]}] got [{sensors[col]}]."
1180                    )
1181
1182        # Readings should have at least one non-null value from expect_types.
1183        allnull = sensors[[x for x in expect_types if x in sensors.columns]].filter(
1184            polars.all_horizontal(polars.all().is_null())
1185        )
1186        missing_count = allnull.shape[0]
1187        if missing_count > 0:
1188            self.logger.info(f"{step} validation: at least one non-null value in readings.")
1189            # Note: Missing values are expected in sensor data (e.g., temperature-only vs humidity-only sensors)
1190            # errs.append(f"{missing_count} missing values in [{col}].")
1191
1192        # Are the SensorReadingUTC close to the QueryUTC (the time the data was requested via API)?
1193        if utc is not None:
1194            maxdiff_minutes = (
1195                numpy.max(numpy.abs(sensors["SensorReadingUTC"].to_numpy() - utc)) / 60
1196            )
1197            if maxdiff_minutes > 5: # readings should be happening every 2 minutes.
1198                errs.append(
1199                    f"SensorReadingUTC is {maxdiff_minutes:,.0f} minutes old"
1200                )
1201            else:                
1202                self.logger.info(
1203                    f"{step} validation passed: SensorReadingUTC columns close to QueryUTC."
1204                )
1205
1206        # Are there any duplicated SensorReadingUTC per SensorID?
1207        if "SensorReadingUTC" in sensors.columns:
1208            dup_count = (
1209                sensors[["SensorID", "SensorReadingUTC"]].is_duplicated().sum()
1210            )
1211            if dup_count > 0:
1212                errs.append(f"Count of duplicated SensorReadingUTC: {dup_count}.")
1213            else:                
1214                self.logger.info(
1215                    f"{step} validation passed: no duplicated SensorReadingUTC per SensorID."
1216                )
1217
1218        # Do any sensors have multiple names (indicating a change in name)?
1219        name_dups = sensors[["SensorID", "SensorName"]].unique()
1220        name_dups = name_dups.filter(name_dups["SensorID"].is_duplicated())
1221        dup_count = name_dups[["SensorID"]].unique().shape[0]
1222        if dup_count > 0:
1223            errs.append(f"Count of multiple names for SensorID: {dup_count}.")
1224        else:            
1225            self.logger.info(f"{step} validation passed: one SensorName per SensorID.")
1226
1227        # Time between readings should be less than ten minutes.
1228        if "SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior" in sensors.columns:
1229            badrows = sensors.filter(
1230                sensors["SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior"] > 60 * 15
1231            )
1232            if badrows.shape[0] > 0:
1233                errs.append(
1234                    f"Count of SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior > 15 minutes: {badrows.shape[0]}."
1235                )
1236            else:                
1237                self.logger.info(
1238                    f"{step} validation passed: SensorReadingUTC_SecondsFromPrior less than 15 minutes."
1239                )
1240
1241        # Comparisons to historical.
1242        if historical.shape[0] > 0:
1243
1244            # Did we lose any sensors?
1245            missing = historical.filter(
1246                historical["SensorID"].is_in(sensors["SensorID"]).not_()
1247            )
1248            if missing.shape[0] > 0:
1249                errs.append(
1250                    f"Count of sensors missing from historical data: {missing.shape[0]}."
1251                )
1252            else:
1253                self.logger.info(
1254                    f"{step} validation passed: all SensorID in historical data (no dropped SensorID)."
1255                )
1256
1257        # Log the errors.
1258        if len(errs) > 0:
1259            self.error(
1260                step + " validation errors : " + "; ".join(errs) + "\n",
1261                raise_exception=False,
1262            )
1263
1264    def validate_devices(self, devices: polars.DataFrame):
1265        """
1266        Validate Device data: column data types, missing values.
1267        Can be expanded to add more validation steps.
1268
1269        Parameters
1270        ----------
1271        devices: polars.DataFrame
1272            Device readings DataFrame to validate.
1273        """
1274
1275        errs = []
1276
1277        # Check for missing values.
1278        # Note: Missing values are expected in sensor data (e.g., temperature-only vs humidity-only sensors)
1279        # for col in self.acceptable_range:
1280        #     missing_count = devices[col].is_null().sum()
1281        #     if missing_count > 0:
1282        #         errs.append(f"{missing_count} missing values in [{col}].")
1283
1284        # Log the errors.
1285        if len(errs) > 0:
1286            self.error(
1287                "Validation errors: \n" + "\n\t".join(errs), raise_exception=False
1288            )
1289
1290    def which(x):
1291        return list(numpy.where(x)[0])
1292
1293    def send_alerts(self, sensors: polars.DataFrame, utc: int):
1294        """
1295        Send alerts based on the sensor data.
1296        Currently, this function saves alerts to "alerts.txt" in the data folder.
1297        Later, this can be connected to an messaging system like Twilio.
1298
1299        Parameters
1300        ----------
1301        sensors: polars.DataFrame
1302            Sensor readings DataFrame.
1303
1304        utc: int
1305            Current UTC timestamp. Passed from another function to keep alerts aligned with QueryUTC.
1306        """
1307
1308        alerts = []
1309        for reading in self.acceptable_range:
1310
1311            if len(self.acceptable_range[reading]) == 0:
1312                continue
1313
1314            reading_idx = self.which(sensors.columns == reading)
1315
1316            for i, row in sensors.iter_rows():
1317                if (not not row[reading_idx].is_null()) and (
1318                    row[reading_idx] < self.acceptable_range[reading][0]
1319                    or row[reading] > self.acceptable_range[reading][1]
1320                ):
1321                    alerts.append(row)
1322
1323        # Write the alerts to a file.
1324        # Later, this can be connected to an alerting system like Twilio.
1325        if len(alerts) > 0:
1326            with open(f"{self.data_path}/alerts.txt", "w") as f:
1327                f.write("\n".join(alerts))
1328
1329    def update_lookups(self):
1330        """
1331        Build (or re-build) the lookup tables used for analytical queries using the consolidated parquet files: sensors, devices, and utcs.
1332        """
1333
1334        # We need some manual fixes to reformat invalid names.
1335        name_overrides = {
1336            "980D Unnamed Temp Sensor": "Temp Unnamed Unnamed_980D",
1337            "980D Unnamed Humid Sensor": "RH Unnamed Unnamed_980D",
1338        }
1339
1340        building_name_map = {
1341            "ESC": "Environmental Science Center",
1342            "YPM": "Yale Peabody Museum",
1343            "KGL": "Kline Geology Laboratory",
1344            "CSC": "Collection Studies Center (West Campus)",
1345        }
1346
1347        # Sensor Info.
1348        columns_to_read = [
1349            "SensorName",
1350            "SensorID",
1351            "DeviceID",
1352            "SensorType",
1353            "Source",
1354        ]
1355        if self.conserv_enabled:
1356            columns_to_read.append("ConservCustomerID")
1357            
1358        sensors_data = polars.read_parquet(
1359            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet",
1360            columns=columns_to_read,
1361        )
1362        sensors_data = sensors_data.unique().to_dicts()
1363        sensors = []
1364        for sensor in sensors_data:
1365
1366            sensorname = sensor["SensorName"]
1367            # Skip processing if SensorName is None/null
1368            if sensorname is None:
1369                continue
1370                
1371            if sensorname in name_overrides:
1372                sensorname = name_overrides[sensorname]
1373
1374            # Fix sensor names with problematic prefixes by removing everything up to and including the first space
1375            if "__" in sensorname and " " in sensorname:
1376                sensorname = sensorname[sensorname.index(" ") + 1:]
1377
1378            # Fix sensor names with " - no comm" suffix
1379            if " - no comm" in sensorname:
1380                sensorname = sensorname.replace(" - no comm", "")
1381
1382            if "floator" in sensorname.lower():
1383                info = sensorname.strip().split("_")
1384            else:
1385                info = sensorname.strip().split(" ")
1386                info = info[0:-1] + info[-1].split("_")
1387            
1388            # Clean up empty strings from consecutive separators (e.g., multiple underscores)
1389            info = [part for part in info if part.strip() != ""]
1390
1391            # If the cardinal direction is included, there will be 4 pieces of info.
1392            if len(info) == 5:
1393                sensors.append(
1394                    {
1395                        "Source": sensor["Source"],
1396                        "SensorName": sensorname,
1397                        #   'SensorType_fromName': info[0],
1398                        "DeviceSerialFromName": info[4],
1399                        "SensorType": sensor["SensorType"],
1400                        "SensorID": sensor["SensorID"],
1401                        "DeviceID": sensor["DeviceID"],
1402                        "BuildingID": info[1],
1403                        "Building": (
1404                            building_name_map[info[1]]
1405                            if info[1] in building_name_map
1406                            else "Unknown"
1407                        ),
1408                        "Room": info[2].replace("_", ""),
1409                        "CardinalDirection": info[3],
1410                    }
1411                )
1412                if info[1] not in building_name_map:
1413                    self.logger.warning(
1414                        f"Building ID {info[1]} not found in building_name_map for sensor {sensorname}"
1415                    )
1416
1417            elif len(info) == 4:
1418
1419                sensors.append(
1420                    {
1421                        "Source": sensor["Source"],
1422                        "SensorName": sensorname,
1423                        #'SensorType_fromName': info[0],
1424                        "DeviceSerialFromName": info[3],
1425                        "SensorType": sensor["SensorType"],
1426                        "SensorID": sensor["SensorID"],
1427                        "DeviceID": sensor["DeviceID"],
1428                        "BuildingID": info[1],
1429                        "Building": (
1430                            building_name_map[info[1]]
1431                            if info[1] in building_name_map
1432                            else "Unknown"
1433                        ),
1434                        "Room": info[2].replace("_", ""),
1435                        "CardinalDirection": "Not Indicated",
1436                    }
1437                )
1438                if info[1] not in building_name_map:
1439                    self.logger.warning(
1440                        f"Building ID {info[1]} not found in building_name_map for sensor {sensorname}"
1441                    )
1442
1443            # Floaters are len 3.
1444            elif len(info) == 3:
1445                sensors.append(
1446                    {
1447                        "Source": sensor["Source"],
1448                        "SensorName": sensorname,
1449                        # 'SensorType_fromName': info[0],
1450                        "DeviceSerialFromName": info[2],
1451                        "SensorType": sensor["SensorType"],
1452                        "SensorID": sensor["SensorID"],
1453                        "DeviceID": sensor["DeviceID"],
1454                        "BuildingID": "FLOATER",
1455                        "Building": (
1456                            building_name_map[info[1]]
1457                            if info[1] in building_name_map
1458                            else "Unknown"
1459                        ),
1460                        "Room": "FLOATER",
1461                        "CardinalDirection": None,
1462                    }
1463                )
1464            else:
1465                # Handle malformed sensor names gracefully with NAs
1466                self.logger.warning(
1467                    f"Malformed SensorName format: {sensorname}. Info: {info}. "
1468                    f"Adding with NA values for parsed fields. "
1469                    f"Valid formats: "
1470                    f"'Temp ESC Room101 North_1234' (5 parts with cardinal direction), "
1471                    f"'RH YPM Gallery_2567' (4 parts without cardinal direction), "
1472                    f"'Temp_Floater ESC_3890' (3 parts for floaters)"
1473                )
1474                sensors.append(
1475                    {
1476                        "Source": sensor["Source"],
1477                        "SensorName": sensorname,
1478                        "DeviceSerialFromName": None,  # NA for malformed names
1479                        "SensorType": sensor["SensorType"],
1480                        "SensorID": sensor["SensorID"], 
1481                        "DeviceID": sensor["DeviceID"],
1482                        "BuildingID": "MALFORMED",
1483                        "Building": "Unknown",
1484                        "Room": "Unknown", 
1485                        "CardinalDirection": None,
1486                    }
1487                )
1488
1489        # Write the table to a file.
1490        sensors = polars.DataFrame(sensors).unique()
1491        sensors = sensors.sort(
1492            ["BuildingID", "Building", "Room", "DeviceSerialFromName", "SensorName"]
1493        )
1494        sensors = self.clean_validate_sensors(sensors=sensors, step="update_lookups")
1495        sensors = self.relocate(
1496            sensors,
1497            ["Source", "SensorID", "SensorName", "SensorType", "DeviceID", "DeviceSerialFromName", "BuildingID", "Building", "Room", "CardinalDirection"],
1498        )
1499        sensors.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/sensors.parquet")
1500
1501        # It will be helpful to have the Building, Room, and CardinalDirection appended to Devices.
1502        # Check for a valid mapping.
1503        device_info_from_sensors = sensors.select(
1504            [
1505                "DeviceID",
1506                "BuildingID",
1507                "Building",
1508                "Room",
1509                "CardinalDirection",
1510                "DeviceSerialFromName",
1511            ]
1512        ).unique()
1513
1514        # Check for inconsistent DeviceID mappings (same DeviceID with different Building/Room/CardinalDirection)
1515        # Group by DeviceID and check if there are multiple unique combinations of Building/Room/CardinalDirection
1516        device_consistency_check = device_info_from_sensors.group_by("DeviceID").agg([
1517            polars.col("BuildingID").n_unique().alias("unique_buildings"),
1518            polars.col("Room").n_unique().alias("unique_rooms"), 
1519            polars.col("CardinalDirection").n_unique().alias("unique_directions")
1520        ])
1521        
1522        inconsistent_devices = device_consistency_check.filter(
1523            (polars.col("unique_buildings") > 1) |
1524            (polars.col("unique_rooms") > 1) |
1525            (polars.col("unique_directions") > 1)
1526        )
1527
1528        if inconsistent_devices.shape[0] > 0:
1529            # Get the actual inconsistent mappings for logging
1530            bad_device_ids = inconsistent_devices.select("DeviceID").to_series().to_list()
1531            bad_values = device_info_from_sensors.filter(
1532                polars.col("DeviceID").is_in(bad_device_ids)
1533            ).sort("DeviceID")
1534            
1535            self.logger.warning(
1536                f"DeviceID has inconsistent Building/Room/CardinalDirection mappings. Using first occurrence: \n{bad_values}"
1537            )
1538            
1539            # Keep only the first occurrence of each DeviceID to maintain consistency
1540            device_info_from_sensors = device_info_from_sensors.group_by("DeviceID").first()
1541        else:
1542            # If all mappings are consistent, we can still have multiple rows per DeviceID (for different sensor types)
1543            # Just keep one representative row per DeviceID since Building/Room/CardinalDirection should be the same
1544            device_info_from_sensors = device_info_from_sensors.group_by("DeviceID").first()
1545
1546        # Device Info.
1547        devices = polars.read_parquet(
1548            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet",
1549            columns=["Source", "DeviceID", "DeviceName"],
1550        ).unique()
1551        devices = devices.join(
1552            device_info_from_sensors, how="left", on="DeviceID"
1553        ).sort(["BuildingID", "Room", "DeviceName"])
1554        
1555        # Get sensor information for each device from the sensors lookup table
1556        device_sensors_lookup = sensors.group_by("DeviceID").agg([
1557            polars.col("SensorID").str.concat(", ").alias("Sensors"),
1558            polars.col("SensorName").str.concat(", ").alias("SensorNames"),
1559            polars.col("SensorType").str.concat(", ").alias("SensorTypes")
1560        ])
1561        
1562        # Join sensor information to devices
1563        devices = devices.join(device_sensors_lookup, how="left", on="DeviceID")
1564        
1565        devices = self.relocate(
1566            devices,
1567            ["Source", "DeviceID", "DeviceName", "Sensors", "SensorNames", "SensorTypes", "DeviceSerialFromName", "BuildingID", "Building", "Room", "CardinalDirection"],
1568        )
1569        devices.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/devices.parquet")
1570
1571        # UTC info.
1572        # Get all UTC timestamps from sensor_readings: both SensorReadingUTC and QueryUTC
1573        # sensor_readings is the primary source since all other data derives from it
1574        
1575        # Read both SensorReadingUTC and QueryUTC columns
1576        utc_data = polars.read_parquet(
1577            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet", 
1578            columns=["SensorReadingUTC", "QueryUTC"]
1579        )
1580        
1581        # Get SensorReadingUTC values (remove nulls)
1582        sensor_reading_utcs = (
1583            utc_data.filter(polars.col("SensorReadingUTC").is_not_null())
1584            ["SensorReadingUTC"]
1585            .unique()
1586            .to_list()
1587        )
1588        
1589        # Get QueryUTC values (remove nulls) 
1590        query_utcs = (
1591            utc_data.filter(polars.col("QueryUTC").is_not_null())
1592            ["QueryUTC"]
1593            .unique()
1594            .to_list()
1595        )
1596        
1597        # Combine all UTC timestamps and get unique values
1598        utc_timestamps = list(set(sensor_reading_utcs + query_utcs))
1599
1600        utcs = polars.DataFrame(
1601            {
1602                "UTC": utc_timestamps,
1603                "datetime_utc": [
1604                    datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(x) for x in utc_timestamps
1605                ],
1606            }
1607        )
1608
1609        # Convert to EST and round to seconds.
1610        utcs = utcs.with_columns(
1611            polars.col("datetime_utc")
1612            .dt.convert_time_zone("America/New_York")
1613            .dt.round("1s")
1614            .alias("datetime_est")
1615        )
1616
1617        # Extract all the date parts.
1618        utcs = utcs.with_columns(
1619            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.date().alias("date"),
1620            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.time().alias("time"),
1621            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.year().alias("year"),
1622            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.month().alias("month"),
1623            (polars.col("datetime_est").dt.strftime("%A")).alias("day_of_week"),
1624            polars.col("datetime_est")
1625            .dt.weekday()
1626            .alias("day_of_week_monday1_sunday7"),
1627            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.hour().alias("hour_24"),
1628            (polars.col("datetime_est").dt.hour() % 12).alias("hour_12"),
1629            polars.col("datetime_est").dt.strftime("%p").alias("am_pm"),
1630        )
1631
1632        # Write the table to a file.
1633        utcs.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/utcs.parquet")
1634
1635    def update_cubes(self):
1636        """
1637        Build (or re-build) the cubed tables using the consolidated parquet files.
1638        Cubes contain aggregated measures by day and device/sensor to facilitate faster queries on smaller files.
1639        In the future, cubes can be modified to include different aggregation levels and dimensions.
1640        """
1641
1642        sumcols = list(self.acceptable_range.keys())
1643        utcs = polars.read_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/utcs.parquet")
1644
1645        sensor_readings = polars.read_parquet(
1646            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet"
1647        )
1648        sensor_readings = sensor_readings.filter(
1649            polars.col("QueryUTC").is_null() | 
1650            ((polars.col("SensorReadingUTC") - polars.col("QueryUTC")).abs() < 60 * 5)
1651        )  # include historical data (QueryUTC=null) and recent readings within 5min window
1652        sensor_readings = sensor_readings.join(
1653            utcs[["UTC", "date"]],
1654            how="left",
1655            left_on="SensorReadingUTC",
1656            right_on="UTC",
1657        )
1658
1659        sensor_readings_daily = (
1660            sensor_readings.group_by(["Source", "date", "SensorID"])
1661            .agg(
1662                [
1663                    polars.len().alias("row_count"),
1664                    polars.col(sumcols).sum().name.suffix("_sum"),
1665                    polars.col(sumcols).min().name.suffix("_min"),
1666                    polars.col(sumcols).max().name.suffix("_max"),
1667                ]
1668            )
1669            .sort(["Source", "date", "SensorID"])
1670        )
1671
1672        sensor_readings_daily.write_parquet(
1673            f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings_daily.parquet"
1674        )
1675
1676        device_readings = polars.read_parquet(
1677            f"{self.data_path}/device_readings.parquet"
1678        )
1679        device_readings = device_readings.filter(
1680            polars.col("QueryUTC").is_null() | 
1681            ((polars.col("SensorReadingUTC") - polars.col("QueryUTC")).abs() < 60 * 5)
1682        )  # include historical data (QueryUTC=null) and recent readings within 5min window
1683        device_readings = device_readings.join(
1684            utcs[["UTC", "date"]],
1685            how="left",
1686            left_on="SensorReadingUTC",
1687            right_on="UTC",
1688        )
1689
1690        device_readings_daily = (
1691            device_readings.group_by(["Source", "date", "DeviceID"])
1692            .agg(
1693                [
1694                    polars.len().alias("row_count"),
1695                    polars.col(sumcols).sum().name.suffix("_sum"),
1696                    polars.col(sumcols).min().name.suffix("_min"),
1697                    polars.col(sumcols).max().name.suffix("_max"),
1698                ]
1699            )
1700            .sort(["Source", "date", "DeviceID"])
1701        )
1702
1703        device_readings_daily.write_parquet(
1704            f"{self.data_path}/device_readings_daily.parquet"
1705        )
EnvironmentData( CatsUserID: int = None, data_path: str = './data/', days_back: int = 730, out_of_scope: list = [], testing: bool = False, coris_enabled: bool = False, conserv_enabled: bool = False, hobolink_enabled: bool = False) 
 15    def __init__(
 16        self,
 17        CatsUserID: int = None,  # Deprecated - now read from environment
 18        data_path: str = "./data/",
 19        days_back: int = int(365 * 2),

 21        testing: bool = False,
 22        coris_enabled: bool = False,

 24        hobolink_enabled: bool = False,

 26        """
 27        Initialize resources for managing the environmental readings.

 29        Parameters

 32            DEPRECATED: Cats User ID is now read from CATS_USER_ID environment variable.
 33            This parameter is maintained for backward compatibility but is ignored.
 34
 35        data_path : str, default='./data/'
 36            Path to store the parquet files which make up the database.
 37
 38        days_back : int, default=int(365 * 2)
 39            Number of days of historical data to pull when initializing the database.
 40
 41        out_of_scope : list[str], default=[]
 42            List of strings indicating sensors that are out of scope and should be ignored.
 43            If a SensorName starts with any of the strings in the list, that Sensor will be ignored.
 44
 45        testing : bool, default=False
 46            Create a class in "testing mode". Only a few sensors will be included so that tests can run quickly and use fewer API calls.
 47
 48        coris_enabled : bool, default=True
 49            Enable Coris API integration for primary sensor data source.
 50
 51        conserv_enabled : bool, default=False
 52            Enable Conserv API integration for additional sensor data sources.
 53
 54        hobolink_enabled : bool, default=False
 55            Enable Hobolink API integration for additional sensor data sources.
 56
 57        Returns
 58        -------
 59        EnvironmentData: EnvironmentData object.
 60        """
 61
 62        # Save inputs to the class instance.
 63        self.CatsUserID = CatsUserID  # Kept for backward compatibility
 64        self.data_path = data_path
 65        self.testing = testing
 66        self.testing_sensor_ids = []
 67        self.out_of_scope = out_of_scope
 68        self.coris_enabled = coris_enabled
 69        self.conserv_enabled = conserv_enabled
 70        self.hobolink_enabled = hobolink_enabled
 71
 72        # Check that at least one data source is enabled
 73        if not (coris_enabled or conserv_enabled or hobolink_enabled):
 74            raise ValueError(
 75                "At least one data source must be enabled. "
 76                "Set coris_enabled=True, conserv_enabled=True, or hobolink_enabled=True"
 77            )
 78
 79        # Create the data folder.
 80        if not os.path.exists(data_path):
 81            os.makedirs(data_path)
 82
 83        # Set up logging to allow status to be viewed when run as a cron job.
 84        # https://docs.python.org/3/howto/logging-cookbook.html#logging-cookbook
 85        self.logger = logging.getLogger("EnvironmentData")
 86        self.logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
 87        formatter = logging.Formatter(
 88            "%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"
 89        )
 90
 91        fh = logging.FileHandler(
 92            f"{data_path}/EnvironmentData.log"
 93        )  # log to EnvironmentData.log in the data folder.
 94        fh.setFormatter(formatter)
 95        self.logger.addHandler(fh)
 96
 97        # ch = logging.StreamHandler() # log to console. disabling to prevent breaking tdqm
 98        # ch.setFormatter(formatter)
 99        # self.logger.addHandler(ch)
100
101        # Set up a second logger for errors only.
102        self.logger_err = logging.getLogger("EnvironmentData-Errors")
103        self.logger_err.setLevel(logging.ERROR)
104        fh = logging.FileHandler(f"{data_path}/EnvironmentData-Errors.log")
105        fh.setFormatter(formatter)
106        self.logger_err.addHandler(fh)
107
108        # Read cron status, or initialize the status file.
109        if os.path.exists(f"{data_path}/cron_status.txt"):
110            with open(f"{data_path}/cron_status.txt") as f:
111                self.cron_status = f.read()
112        else:
113            self.update_cron_status("not-initialized")
114
115        # Initialize Coris API client if enabled
116        self.coris_client = None
117        if self.coris_enabled:
118            try:
119                self.coris_client = create_coris_client_from_env(self.logger)
120                # self.logger.info("Coris API client initialized successfully")
121            except Exception as e:
122                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to initialize Coris client: {e}")
123                self.coris_enabled = False
124
125        # Initialize Conserv API client if enabled
126        self.conserv_client = None
127        if self.conserv_enabled:
128            try:
129                self.conserv_client = create_conserv_client_from_env(self.logger)
130                # self.logger.info(
131                #     f"Conserv API client initialized with {len(self.conserv_client.customers)} customers"
132                # )
133            except Exception as e:
134                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to initialize Conserv client: {e}")
135                self.conserv_enabled = False
136
137        # Initialize Hobolink API client if enabled
138        self.hobolink_client = None
139        if self.hobolink_enabled:
140            try:
141                self.hobolink_client = HobolinkClient(self.logger)
142                # self.logger.info("Hobolink API client initialized successfully")
143            except Exception as e:
144                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to initialize Hobolink client: {e}")
145                print(f"DEBUG: Failed to initialize Hobolink client: {e}")
146                self.hobolink_enabled = False
147
148        # Set up the readings data structure that will be used throughout.
149        self.acceptable_range = {"SensorReadingF": [], "SensorReadingRh": []}
150
151        # Debug: Show which data sources are actually enabled
152        enabled_sources = []
153        if self.coris_enabled and self.coris_client:
154            enabled_sources.append("Coris")
155        if self.conserv_enabled and self.conserv_client:
156            enabled_sources.append("Conserv") 
157        if self.hobolink_enabled and self.hobolink_client:
158            enabled_sources.append("Hobolink")
159        
160        print(f"DEBUG: Enabled data sources: {enabled_sources}")
161        self.logger.info(f"Enabled data sources: {enabled_sources}")
162
163        # Initialize the database by creating a parquet file for each reading type and populate it with historical data.
164        self.initialize_database(days_back=days_back)

def update_cron_status(self, status: str): 
167    def update_cron_status(self, status: str):
168        """
169        cron_status is used to prevent new cron-triggered API queries during initialization while the historical data is being pulled. Update the status of the cron job.
170        There are only two statuses: "not-initialized" and "initialized".
171        This function updates the status by writing to "cron_status.txt" and setting the class instance variable self.cron_status.
172
173        Parameters
174        ----------
175        status : str {"not-initialized", "initialized"}
176            New status of the cron job.
177        """
178
179        self.cron_status = status
180        with open(f"{self.data_path}/cron_status.txt", "w") as f:
181            f.write(status)

def close(self): 
183    def close(self):
184        """
185        Close the class.
186        Disconnects the connection to the log files so they can be deleted, etc.
187        """
188
189        for handler in self.logger.handlers:
190            handler.close()
191            self.logger.removeHandler(handler)
192        del self.logger
193
194        for handler in self.logger_err.handlers:
195            handler.close()
196            self.logger_err.removeHandler(handler)
197        del self.logger_err

def error(self, msg, raise_exception=False): 
199    def error(self, msg, raise_exception=False):
200        """
201        Helper function for errors.
202        Logs an error message to the both log files (error regular) and raises an exception if you choose.
203
204        Parameters
205        ----------
206        msg : str
207            Error message.
208
209        raise_exception : bool, default=False
210            If True, log the error and raise an exception, which will halt processing. If False, log the error, generate a warning, and continue processing.
211        """
212
213        self.logger_err.error(msg)
214        self.logger.error(msg)
215
216        if raise_exception:
217            raise Exception(msg)
218        else:
219            warnings.warn(msg)

def initialize_database(self, days_back: int): 
221    def initialize_database(self, days_back: int):
222        """
223        Get and save historical data for each sensor.
224
225        Parameters
226        ----------
227        days_back : int
228            Number of days of historical data to pull.
229        """
230
231        # If the data already exists, initialization is not necessary.
232        if self.cron_status != "not-initialized":
233            return
234
235        # Make a log entry and gather current and starting UTC.
236        # self.logger.info("initialize_database")
237        current_utc = self.get_current_utc()
238        start_utc = current_utc - days_back * 24 * 60 * 60
239
240        # ============ CORIS HISTORICAL DATA PROCESSING ============
241        readings = []
242        if self.coris_enabled and self.coris_client:
243            # Get historical data from Coris API using the client
244            coris_readings = self.coris_client.get_historical_data(
245                acceptable_range=self.acceptable_range,
246                start_utc=start_utc,
247                end_utc=current_utc,
248                out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
249                testing=self.testing,
250                testing_sensor_ids=self.testing_sensor_ids
251            )
252
253            # Clean and validate the Coris data
254            for i, data in enumerate(coris_readings):
255                coris_readings[i] = self.clean_validate_sensors(
256                    sensors=data, step="initialize_database"
257                )
258            
259            readings.extend(coris_readings)
260
261        # ============ CONSERV HISTORICAL DATA PROCESSING ============
262        conserv_readings = []
263        if self.conserv_enabled and self.conserv_client:
264            self.logger.info("Fetching Conserv historical data for all customers")
265
266            try:
267                # Get Conserv data for the same time period as Coris
268                conserv_data = self.conserv_client.get_data_for_period(
269                    start_utc=start_utc,
270                    end_utc=current_utc,
271                    max_concurrent_jobs=3 if self.testing else 5,
272                )
273
274                if conserv_data is not None and not conserv_data.is_empty():
275                    # Conserv data is already transformed by modules/conserv_client.py
276                    # Clean and validate Conserv data
277                    conserv_data = self.clean_validate_sensors(
278                        sensors=conserv_data, step="initialize_database_conserv"
279                    )
280
281                    # Add to readings list
282                    conserv_readings.append(conserv_data)
283                    self.logger.info(
284                        f"Successfully processed {conserv_data.shape[0]} Conserv historical records"
285                    )
286                else:
287                    self.logger.info(
288                        "No Conserv historical data available for the specified period"
289                    )
290
291            except Exception as e:
292                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch Conserv historical data: {e}")
293                # Continue without Conserv data - don't fail the entire initialization
294
295        # ============ HOBOLINK HISTORICAL DATA PROCESSING ============
296        hobolink_readings = []
297        if self.hobolink_enabled and self.hobolink_client:
298            # print("DEBUG: Fetching Hobolink historical data")
299            # self.logger.info("Fetching Hobolink historical data")
300            
301            try:
302                # Get Hobolink data for the same time period
303                hobolink_data_list = self.hobolink_client.get_historical_data(
304                    start_utc=start_utc,
305                    end_utc=current_utc,
306                    out_of_scope=self.out_of_scope,
307                    testing=self.testing
308                )
309                
310                if hobolink_data_list is not None and len(hobolink_data_list) > 0:
311                    # Clean and validate each DataFrame in the list
312                    total_records = 0
313                    for i, data in enumerate(hobolink_data_list):
314                        if data is not None and not data.is_empty():
315                            hobolink_data_list[i] = self.clean_validate_sensors(
316                                sensors=data, step="initialize_database_hobolink"
317                            )
318                            total_records += hobolink_data_list[i].shape[0]
319                    
320                    # Add all DataFrames to readings list
321                    hobolink_readings.extend(hobolink_data_list)
322                    # print(f"DEBUG: Successfully processed {total_records} Hobolink historical records from {len(hobolink_data_list)} DataFrames")
323                    # self.logger.info(
324                    #     f"Successfully processed {total_records} Hobolink historical records from {len(hobolink_data_list)} DataFrames"
325                    # )
326                else:
327                    print("DEBUG: No Hobolink historical data available for the specified period")
328                    self.logger.info(
329                        "No Hobolink historical data available for the specified period"
330                    )
331                    
332            except Exception as e:
333                print(f"DEBUG: Failed to fetch Hobolink historical data: {e}")
334                self.logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch Hobolink historical data: {e}")
335                # Continue without Hobolink data - don't fail the entire initialization
336        else:
337            print(f"DEBUG: Hobolink not enabled or client not initialized. Enabled: {self.hobolink_enabled}, Client: {self.hobolink_client}")
338
339        # ============ COMBINE ALL DATA SOURCES ============
340        # Combine Coris, Conserv, and Hobolink readings into a single polars DataFrame
341        all_readings = readings + conserv_readings + hobolink_readings
342        dt = (
343            polars.concat(all_readings, how="diagonal")
344            if all_readings
345            else polars.DataFrame()
346        )
347
348        if dt.is_empty():
349            error_msg = "No data from any source - initialization failed"
350            self.logger.error(error_msg)
351            raise RuntimeError(error_msg)
352
353        # Standardize the DataFrame (rename columns, filter, and reorder)
354        dt = self.standardize_sensor_dataframe(dt)
355
356        # Write the database file.
357        dt.write_parquet(f"{self.data_path}/sensor_readings.parquet")
358        self.logger.info(
359            f"Historical data initialization complete: {dt.shape[0]} total records from {len(all_readings)} sources"
360        )
361
362        self.update_cron_status("initialized")

def enforce_schema( self, df: polars.dataframe.frame.DataFrame, step_name: str = '') -> polars.dataframe.frame.DataFrame: 
453    def enforce_schema(
454        self, df: polars.DataFrame, step_name: str = ""
455    ) -> polars.DataFrame:
456        """
457        SCHEMA GATE: Enforce master schema on any DataFrame before concatenation.
458        This prevents ALL type mismatch errors by converting data to expected types.
459
460        Parameters
461        ----------
462        df : polars.DataFrame
463            DataFrame to enforce schema on
464        step_name : str
465            Name of the step for logging
466
467        Returns
468        -------
469        polars.DataFrame
470            DataFrame with all columns converted to master schema types
471        """
472
473        if df.is_empty():
474            return df
475
476        master_schema = self.get_master_schema()
477
478        # Track conversions for logging
479        conversions_made = []
480
481        # Apply schema enforcement
482        conversion_exprs = []
483        failed = False
484
485        for column in df.columns:
486            if column in master_schema:
487                target_type = master_schema[column]
488                current_type = df[column].dtype
489
490                if current_type != target_type:
491                    conversions_made.append(
492                        f"{column}: {current_type} -> {target_type}"
493                    )
494
495                    try:
496                        # Handle specific conversion cases
497                        if target_type == polars.Null:
498                            # Keep null columns as-is
499                            continue
500                        elif str(current_type).startswith("Int") and str(
501                            target_type
502                        ).startswith("Int"):
503                            # Int64 -> Int32 or vice versa (check for overflow)
504                            conversion_exprs.append(
505                                polars.col(column).cast(target_type, strict=False)
506                            )
507                        elif str(current_type).startswith("Float") and str(
508                            target_type
509                        ).startswith("Float"):
510                            # Float64 -> Float32 or vice versa
511                            conversion_exprs.append(
512                                polars.col(column).cast(target_type)
513                            )
514                        else:
515                            # Generic conversion
516                            conversion_exprs.append(
517                                polars.col(column).cast(target_type, strict=False)
518                            )
519
520                    except Exception as conv_error:
521                        self.logger.error(
522                            f"Schema validation failed for {step_name}: Failed to convert {column}: {conv_error}"
523                        )
524                        failed = True
525                        # Keep original column if conversion fails
526                        continue
527
528        # Apply all conversions at once
529        if conversion_exprs:
530            df = df.with_columns(conversion_exprs)
531
532        if not failed:
533            self.logger.info(f"validation passed for {step_name}: Schema enforcement completed")
534
535        return df

SCHEMA GATE: Enforce master schema on any DataFrame before concatenation. This prevents ALL type mismatch errors by converting data to expected types.
